clm-stanford-university-bca-honor-code-f.text: Stanford BCA guidance treats generative AI like assistance from another person when an instructor has not stated a policy. Using AI to substantially complete an assignment or exam is not permitted in that default context. Students should acknowledge non-incidental AI use and disclose when in doubt. Instructors may set course policies.

evidence.quote: Absent a clear statement from a course instructor, use of or consultation with generative AI shall be treated analogously to assistance from another person. In particular, using generative AI tools to substantially complete an assignment or exam (e.g. by entering exam or assignment questions) is not permitted. Students should acknowledge the use of generative AI (other than incidental use) and default to disclosing such assistance when in doubt.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 108; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

clm-stanford-university-gsb-ai-policy.text: For Stanford Graduate School of Business (GSB) MBA and MSx courses, instructors may not ban student use of AI tools for take-home coursework, including assignments and exams. Instructors may choose whether to allow AI for in-class work. For PhD and undergraduate courses, GSB follows the university-wide Generative AI Policy Guidance from the Office of Community Standards.

evidence.quote: MBA/MSx courses: Instructors may not ban student use of AI tools for take-home coursework, including assignments and exams. Instructors may choose whether to allow student use of AI tools for in-class work, including exams. Except for in-class exams, students should be allowed to use AI tools in cases where they are able to use the internet and electronic devices. In-class assignments for which electronic devices are prohibited inherently also prohibit use of the internet, AI tools, tablets, laptops, calculators, etc.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 72; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

evidence.quote: PhD/Undergraduate courses: Follow the Generative AI Policy Guidance from Stanford’s Office of Community Standards.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 73; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

clm-stanford-university-md-ai-policy.text: Stanford School of Medicine MD and MSPA programs have a formal AI policy: students may use AI for learning, clarification, and grammar/style editing unless contrary to assignment instructions. AI use for closed-book exams or assignments where internet is restricted is prohibited unless explicitly authorized by faculty. Students are responsible for all AI-generated content they submit, must disclose and cite substantial AI contributions, and violations may result in disciplinary action.

evidence.quote: Assessments: The use of AI tools is discouraged for any activities in which students are evaluated on their own knowledge or skills, unless explicitly granted permission by the faculty. Unless explicitly advised by individual instructors, the use of AI tools is prohibited for any “closed book” exams or assignments where internet use is restricted.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 122; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

evidence.quote: Learning and Clarification: Students may utilize AI to enhance their understanding of medical concepts, definitions, and for grammar/style editing, provided it does not conflict with specific assignment instructions or be inconsistent with faculty-authorized tasks as detailed below.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 111; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

evidence.quote: Any substantial contributions from AI tools on assignments, presentations, and scholarly abstracts or proposals must be disclosed and properly cited. This includes the tool name, model/version, date, query, and output excerpt. For example: ChatGPT (GPT-4; June 10, 2025), prompt: “Explain ARDS pathophysiology,” output used in Section 2.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 127; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

evidence.quote: AI tools may not be listed as authors on scholarly works.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 128; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

clm-stanford-university-md-phi-prohibiti.text: Stanford Medicine and UIT strictly prohibit entering Protected Health Information (PHI) into consumer, personal, or unauthorized AI tools. Stanford AI Playground is approved for High-Risk non-PHI data; PHI review is in progress. PHI is permissible only within Stanford enterprise services explicitly approved for PHI under university Data Risk Assessment (DRA) and Business Associate Agreement (BAA) safeguards, currently including Stanford-managed ChatGPT Edu and Gemini Enterprise when logged in via Single Sign On with a Stanford-provided account. Claude for Education is approved for High Risk non-PHI data only; PHI processing is not covered. Institutional data approval does not grant clinical or coursework permission.

evidence.quote: To ensure that patient confidentiality is maintained at all times, no confidential research, patient data, or other protected health information (PHI) is to be entered into public AI platforms (e.g., ChatGPT, Gemini, OpenEvidence, Doximity, etc.).
evidence.location: Captured official text line 118; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

evidence.quote: High-Risk non-PHI only; PHI review in progress for AI Playground.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 225; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

evidence.quote: Only approved for use with Stanford data when using a Stanford provided account through the UIT managed ChatGPT Edu service and logged in via Single Sign On.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 205; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

clm-stanford-university-pwr-genai-policy.text: Stanford's Program in Writing and Rhetoric (PWR) prohibits students from using generative AI or LLMs to compose drafts or revisions for any major assignment in PWR courses, including composing or revising portions of essays or scripts, including paraphrases of LLM-generated writing. Students may not rely on generative AI summaries of sources. Violation of PWR's AI policy is treated as an Honor Code violation and results in involvement of the Office of Community Standards.

evidence.quote: Students may not use generative AI or LLMs to compose the drafts or revisions for any of the major assignments in their PWR classes. This includes using generative AI to compose or revise portions of their essay or scripts (from individual phrases or sentences to longer passages) or including in their essays/scripts paraphrases of LLM-generated writing or paraphrases of source material generated by LLMs. In addition, students may not rely on generative AI summaries of sources for their research and instead must actively read and engage themselves with the sources they draw on for their research projects and that they incorporate into their writing.
evidence.location: Captured official text line 103; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

evidence.quote: Violation of PWR’s AI policy is considered an Honor Code violation and will result in the involvement of Stanford’s Office of Community Standards (OCS).
evidence.location: Captured official text line 105; HTML text extraction; raw source retained privately

topicBasis.research_publication: Oxford research policy says substantive discrete-tool use should be declared, with prompts/outputs made available where relevant. MPLS supporting-code rules apply only when coding is not substantive output; debugging is exempt from declaration.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Unauthorised AI use falls under plagiarism and cheating regulations handled by the Proctors. Oxford does not endorse commercial digital AI writing detection tools for disciplinary determinations.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Staff must clearly declare whether and how AI can be used in summative assessments, ensure baseline tool equality when required, and design assessments around the University's three core principles.
topicBasis.security_procurement: Detailed public security guidance has migrated to successor University channels. Current assessment, custom-GPT and bot conditions were not retrieved; historical guidance is not a current procurement or data approval.

It does not approve Level 4 data. HMS separately lists special-request Level 4 tools and a Level 2 ceiling for automated meeting assistants. Product access, data approval, DUA/sponsor limits and assessment permission must be checked separately.

Separate HMS Level 4 research/development services require their own access and data-use conditions.

evidence.quote: Faculty should be clear with students they’re teaching and advising about their policies on permitted uses, if any, of generative AI in classes and on academic work. Students are also encouraged to ask their instructors for clarification about these policies as needed.

clm-harvard-university-hgse-academic-int.text: HGSE states that, unless the instructor specifies otherwise, using generative AI to create all or part of a course assignment and submit it as one’s own violates its Academic Integrity Policy. Permissible learning uses include clarification, brainstorming and contextual scenarios; students must discuss uncertain uses with the instructor before use.

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise specified by your instructor, it is a violation of the HGSE Academic Integrity Policy to use generative AI to create all or part of an assignment for a course (e.g., a paper, memo, presentation, or short response) and submit it as your own.

clm-harvard-university-hgse-attribution.text: For permitted GenAI use in HGSE assignments, students must acknowledge and document the tools used, prompts if applicable, and how outputs were integrated. Direct citations must use proper citation format.

evidence.quote: For any permitted use of GenAI tools, you must acknowledge and document that use in your assignment submission by explaining what tool(s) you used, prompts you provided (if applicable), and how you integrated the output into your work. If you cite directly from the tool, use proper citation format to credit the source.
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 82-82; exact character range 3943:4263; original source representation retained

clm-harvard-university-social-studies-de.text: Social Studies prohibits generative or agentic AI assistance in submitted coursework, exams/quizzes and all thesis stages by default. Instructors may publish alternative syllabus rules but must require disclosure. Thesis exceptions are case-specific: obtain supervisor approval, submit the AI Policy Attestation request, and secure DUS approval by November 1 of senior year, or April 1 for off-cycle fall seniors. The AI Policy Attestation form is required in consultation with the supervisor at Prospectus submission and again in senior year. Thesis work cannot reuse AI-assisted work from another course merely because that course allowed it. These rules apply to Social Studies requirements.

evidence.quote: Policy: the use of generative or agentic AI in any form is prohibited for aid in analyzing, idea-generation, research, formatting, organizing, outlining, drafting, revising, or editing any work submitted in Social Studies courses or other concentration requirements.
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 90-90; exact character range 2376:2642; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: This includes, but is not limited to, papers or responses or posts of any kind or length, in-class presentations, exams and quizzes, preparatory work for the senior thesis (e.g., the Prospectus), research and analysis for the senior thesis, and the drafting, editing, or revising of the senior thesis.
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 91-91; exact character range 2643:2944; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Scope: The Policy serves as the default AI policy for all Social Studies courses, including any for which there is no explicitly stated AI policy. Individual instructors may utilize an alternative AI policy if they deem it pedagogically appropriate. Instructors will notify students in writing of any alternative policy on the syllabus and must require students to disclose the use of AI in all assignment submissions (e.g., a prefatory statement or footnotes throughout).
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 92-92; exact character range 2945:3417; original source representation retained

topicBasis.privacy_data: Educational and research data rules apply in their own contexts. Staff administrative guidance explicitly excludes student learning, assessment and research. Examiners may not upload student work to GenAI.
topicBasis.approved_tools: University Workspace offers Gemini and NotebookLM. Standard Microsoft licences include Copilot Chat at no extra cost for most staff/students; paid M365 integration has account conditions. Access does not grant assessment permission.
topicBasis.research_publication: RDM framework version 4 requires research data and AI-use considerations across the research community. Its statement that there is no distinct GenAI research policy does not establish unrestricted use.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Academic integrity and detector guidance have specific scopes. General discipline/appeal procedures remain unreviewed.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Faculty/course communication and student-work consent constraints apply in the stated contexts.
topicBasis.security_procurement: Review, procurement and risk assessment depend on the actual task, unit and data classification; staff administration is not student assessment.

do.en: Check the Faculty, College and assessment brief before use.

do.en: Check Engineering’s preparation-use declaration and task-specific exceptions.
do.zh: 核对工程考核的准备阶段披露及任务例外。

do.en: For research, follow the RDM framework and funder/publisher requirements.

dont.en: Do not present unacknowledged AI assessment content as your own unless the brief explicitly provides otherwise.
dont.zh: 不得把未注明 AI 考核内容冒充原创，任务明确例外除外。

dont.en: Examiners must not upload student work to GenAI for analysis or feedback.
dont.zh: 考官不得上传学生作品供 AI 分析或反馈。

dont.en: Do not treat staff administrative guidance as universal student assessment rules.
dont.zh: 不要把员工行政指南套为学生考核通则。

claim-cam-assessment-1.text: A student using any unacknowledged content generated by artificial intelligence within a summative assessment as though it is their own work constitutes academic misconduct, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the assessment brief.

evidence.quote: “A student using any unacknowledged content generated by artificial intelligence within a summative assessment as though it is their own work constitutes academic misconduct, unless explicitly stated otherwise in the assessment brief.” Plagiarism & Academic Misconduct
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 119-119; exact character range 2777:3045; original source representation retained

claim-cam-assessment-3.text: Cambridge says examiners across undergraduate, taught-postgraduate and research-postgraduate programmes may not upload, copy or share student work with GenAI/LLMs or use them to analyse submissions and produce feedback. The source also prohibits sharing student IP/submissions without student permission because of uncertain storage/use. Examiners may use AI to support their own feedback writing, such as consolidating personal notes or rephrasing comments; this is not blanket permission to upload student work.

evidence.quote: Examiners across all programmes of study (including Undergraduate, Postgraduate Taught, and Postgraduate Research) are not permitted to upload, copy, or share student work with Generative AI (GenAI) tools and Large Language Models (LLMs).
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 130-130; exact character range 5103:5341; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Examiners may not use tools, such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Google Bard, or Microsoft Copilot, to analyse work submitted by students and provide written feedback.
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 130-130; exact character range 5342:5502; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Due to lack of clarity and uncertainty of how these tools use and/or store input data, it is not permitted to share student IP and submitted work without permission from the student.
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 130-130; exact character range 5503:5685; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Where preferred, however, examiners may use these tools to support their own writing in the process of documenting feedback (e.g., consolidating personal notes and rephrasing comments).
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 131-131; exact character range 5686:5871; original source representation retained

claim-cam-education-1.text: Cambridge broadly permits appropriate GenAI use for personal study, research and formative work, with nuanced Department, Faculty or College guidance controlling the context. Students should check local rules with staff; this is not blanket permission for summative assessments.

evidence.quote: The University of Cambridge broadly permits the appropriate use of GenAI tools and related software, however, due to the variety of disciplines and research areas present at the institution, there is need for more nuanced guidance at local levels.
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 133-133; exact character range 6450:6697; original source representation retained

evidence.quote: Students are permitted to make appropriate use of GenAI tools to support their personal study, research and formative work. Appropriate use is better defined locally by Department, Faculty, or College depending on the context and you should always check with a member of staff to be sure you know how you are able to use these tools for your education. General guidance for use of GenAI is available as well as specific guidance for assessment-related queries.
evidence.location: Derived source text lines 135-135; exact character range 6941:7401; original source representation retained

claim-cam-engineering-genai-assessment-2.text: The Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering Triposes’ policy, approved by the Faculty Board in June 2026, requires declaring all GenAI used to prepare summative work unless the assessment brief states otherwise. Assignment-specific rules take precedence. Students must not generate raw submission/presentation content without an initial self-written base or automatically generate references from content; tools managing student-identified references remain allowed. Students are responsible for submitted work and are expected to explain it; marks reflect unmet learning outcomes even when no academic misconduct is established.

It is not an unconditional privacy prohibition for all student AI use.

Relevant issues include sensitive data, ownership, copyright, ethics, integrity and security. The framework says there is no distinct University GenAI research policy; that does not mean research has no AI-related rules.

evidence.quote: Complying with any requirements from the University, research funders, or publishers when using Generative AI as a tool when undertaking or disseminating research, or when applying for funding, or in the assessment of research.

eth-zurich.name: ETH Zurich (Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich)

scope.en: Read each cited rule for its course, academic unit, activity and exceptions. Site advice does not create a university obligation.
scope.zh: 逐项核对来源中的课程、院系、活动及例外；本站建议不创设校方义务。

coursework.en: ETH Zurich advocates a proactive and responsible approach to generative AI in coursework. Students remain fully responsible for the content of any work they submit. Generative AI may serve a supplementary role (such as brainstorming, structuring, or coding assistance), but must never replace personal effort. Lecturers hold authority to determine whether and how generative AI may be used in their courses.
coursework.zh: AI 只能辅助，不能替代个人工作；学生对提交内容负责，教师决定课程及考核中的使用方式。
coursework.meaningEn: Follow the cited course, supervisor, degree, research or service-specific conditions; local reviewed candidate, not a published student snapshot.
coursework.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

exams.en: Performance assessments must be conducted independently and personally by the student. The use of unauthorized aids, including generative AI tools not permitted by the examiner, constitutes academic misconduct subject to disciplinary action under the ETH Zurich Ordinance on Disciplinary Measures.
exams.zh: 考核须由学生独立亲自完成；使用未经考官许可的 AI 等辅助工具可能依现有纪律程序处理。
exams.meaningEn: Follow the cited course, supervisor, degree, research or service-specific conditions; local reviewed candidate, not a published student snapshot.
exams.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

disclosure.en: ETH Zurich's declaration of originality provides two options: confirming that no generative AI was used, or confirming that authorised generative AI was used and its disclosure agreed with the supervisor. Bachelor's and Master's theses require a signed declaration of originality, while requirements for other written assessments depend on the applicable academic instructions. Doctoral candidates declare independent authorship through the doctoral examination registration process. The permitted use, disclosure format and any exceptions must follow the relevant supervisor and unit requirements. ETH Zurich's teaching guidelines instruct students to be transparent about their use of generative AI and to identify which tools contributed to which parts of their work, in accordance with applicable lecturer instructions and citation conventions. For scientific writing and theses, students should agree in advance with their supervisors on authorised AI use and disclosure requirements. ETH Library guidance recognises an exception where a supervisor has expressly agreed that particular AI use need not be separately declared. In the absence of such an agreement, undeclared use may constitute a breach of academic integrity.
disclosure.zh: 本科与硕士论文须签署原创声明，并与导师约定获准 AI 的披露方式；其他作业及博士声明依相应要求，明确约定可有例外。
disclosure.meaningEn: Follow the cited course, supervisor, degree, research or service-specific conditions; local reviewed candidate, not a published student snapshot.
disclosure.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

privacy_data.en: Uploading strictly confidential information to external cloud AI services is prohibited. Confidential information may only be processed in specifically evaluated configurations (such as M365 Copilot Work mode without web search). M365 Copilot Chat is approved for internal data. Google AI tools have not yet been assessed by the CISO (assessment OPEN) and are not released for ETH confidential, strictly confidential, or protected personal data. Copyright and privacy must be respected at all times.
privacy_data.zh: 严格机密资料不得进入外部云 AI；机密资料仅可用获准配置。Google 工具安全评估仍未完成，产品开放不代表数据批准。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Follow the cited course, supervisor, degree, research or service-specific conditions; local reviewed candidate, not a published student snapshot.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

approved_tools.en: ETH Zurich recommends Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini, and Google NotebookLM for teaching purposes. Base chat versions are included in institutional Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace subscriptions free of charge for students and employees, offering enterprise data protection where user data is not used for model training. Google tools have not yet completed CISO assessment (OPEN), so product availability does not constitute data classification approval. Tool availability does not equal assessment permission; instructors decide assessment permissions.
approved_tools.zh: 机构基础聊天服务可免费提供给学生与员工；教学推荐不构成考核许可，Google 工具也未获保密及受保护个人数据批准。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Follow the cited course, supervisor, degree, research or service-specific conditions; local reviewed candidate, not a published student snapshot.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

research_publication.en: Researchers and students are fully responsible for the integrity of their scientific work and must verify AI-generated output, references, and facts. Generative AI tools cannot be listed as authors or cited as authoritative sources. Theses require signed originality declarations; doctoral candidates declare independent authorship upon registration for the doctoral examination. Researchers must comply with applicable funder (e.g. SNSF) and publisher guidelines.
research_publication.zh: 研究者须核实输出、文献及事实，不能把 AI 列为作者或权威来源；遵守论文声明、资助方及出版要求。
research_publication.meaningEn: Follow the cited course, supervisor, degree, research or service-specific conditions; local reviewed candidate, not a published student snapshot.
research_publication.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

academic_integrity.en: ETH Library provides Turnitin Originality to eligible professors and lecturers for text-similarity checking, subject to data classification and responsible selective-use guidance. Only public or internal documents may be uploaded. Similarity screening is distinct from AI-authorship detection; ETH Zurich warns that technical detection of AI-generated output is unreliable and should not be treated as conclusive evidence. Violations of GenAI guidelines such as use of unauthorised aids or non-disclosure of their use are subject to disciplinary action under existing performance assessment rules and the declaration of originality.
academic_integrity.zh: Turnitin 相似度筛查只可上传公开或内部资料，不能等同 AI 作者检测；学校指出 AI 检测不可靠，违规按现有纪律规则处理。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Applicable units, audience and service modes are as identified in the bound original excerpts.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

teaching_guidance.en: Lecturers are encouraged to adapt teaching and assessment strategies to GenAI, discuss acceptable use with students, clearly communicate course permissions, and act as role models by making GenAI use visible in teaching materials and assessment workflows, ensuring compliance with data protection regulations.
teaching_guidance.zh: 鼓励教师调整教学考核、说明课程许可并透明呈现自身 AI 使用，同时遵守数据保护。
teaching_guidance.meaningEn: Applicable units, audience and service modes are as identified in the bound original excerpts.
teaching_guidance.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

security_procurement.en: ID CCR Cloud Service Center manages institutional cloud AI tools. Tools lacking cloud assessments (including third-party tools such as commercial ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Perplexity, Grok) are used on the user's own responsibility and must never process confidential, strictly confidential, or protected personal data. Institutional add-on software (such as Google AI Pro or M365 Copilot) requires employee license acquisition via the IT-Shop; specific fee and funding arrangements depend on applicable organizational procedures.
security_procurement.zh: 未完成云评估的工具不得处理机密、严格机密或受保护个人数据；附加许可须按 IT-Shop 等适用程序获取。

clm-eth-zurich-ai-data-classification-20.text: ETH Zurich prohibits the processing of strictly confidential information in external cloud AI services. Confidential information may be processed only in services and configurations explicitly approved for that classification. ETH IT guidance distinguishes Microsoft 365 Copilot Work mode without web search, which is approved for confidential data, from Copilot Chat and web mode, which are approved for internal data. Unassessed AI services must not be used for confidential ETH data or protected personal data.

evidence.quote: Uploading strictly confidential data to external cloud services, including AI tools, is prohibited. The work mode of M365 Copilot without the web search option is approved for use with confidential data . The web search option is disabled in the work mode by default. clm-eth-zurich-research-genai-authorship.text: ETH Library guidance requires researchers to remain responsible for their scientific work and to verify AI-generated information, references and quotations. Generative AI tools cannot be listed as scientific authors or relied upon as authoritative scientific sources. Researchers should agree on permitted AI use with collaborators and follow applicable departmental, funder, publisher and journal requirements. Disclosure of an AI tool's contribution is distinct from citing that tool as evidence for a scientific claim.

evidence.quote: In terms of external page copyright law (Article 2), this does not constitute a new work, which is why these tools cannot be considered as authors or co-authors. Furthermore, as this output is neither reproducible nor reliable, generative AI and AI-based tools are not eligible and citation-worthy sources.

scope.en: Read each cited rule for its course, academic unit, activity and exceptions. Site advice does not create a university obligation.
scope.zh: 逐项核对来源中的课程、院系、活动及例外；本站建议不创设校方义务。

coursework.en: AI tools are permitted by default for unsupervised take-home coursework with mandatory disclosure. Work must be the student's own, and quality is evaluated independently of AI use. Course designers hold pedagogical discretion to tailor rules based on learning outcomes.
coursework.zh: 非监督课外考核默认允许 AI，须注明且作品仍为学生本人所作；教师可按学习目标调整规则。
coursework.meaningEn: University teaching and learning; the course instructor’s assessment rules apply.
coursework.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

exams.en: If instructors decide students should be forbidden from using AI for an assessment (for pedagogical reasons), crucial aspects of that assessment should be conducted in person and under instructor supervision. AI detector verdicts are inadmissible as evidence in disciplinary processes or to penalize work.
exams.zh: 教师因教学目的禁止 AI 时，考核关键部分应在现场受监督完成；这是 should，并非所有部分必须现场。检测结果不得作为相关纪律证据或扣罚理由。
exams.meaningEn: University teaching and learning; the course instructor’s assessment rules apply.
exams.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

disclosure.en: Explicit acknowledgement of AI assistance is required for all submitted academic work where AI was used, specifying the tool and nature of assistance according to style guide conventions and course guidelines.
disclosure.zh: 使用 AI 的提交作品须注明工具与辅助方式，并遵守课程及引用格式要求。
disclosure.meaningEn: University teaching and learning; the course instructor’s assessment rules apply.
disclosure.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

privacy_data.en: Instructors should use NUS-approved AI tools whenever NUS data is involved (Section 2.3). ChatGPT Edu provides a university-managed workspace where conversations and data are not used to train OpenAI models; however, uploading sensitive, confidential, or legally protected university data is NOT verified as approved without specific institutional data classification. In no circumstances should AI tool accounts be shared; using a shared account may raise collusion concerns and, where misconduct is established, may result in disciplinary action.
privacy_data.zh: 涉及 NUS 数据时教师应使用获准工具。ChatGPT Edu 不用工作区数据训练模型，不代表已批准敏感数据；不得共享账号。
privacy_data.meaningEn: University teaching and learning; the course instructor’s assessment rules apply.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

approved_tools.en: ChatGPT Edu is announced for campus-wide availability to all students, staff, and faculty starting 31 August 2026. In-house AI-Know tools are primarily staff-focused, while students have access to CFG AI-Xplore via the Marketplace tab, and AI Sense Maker was announced (scheduled 20 August 2026) for research literature discovery. Tool access does not constitute course assessment permission.
approved_tools.zh: 公告称自 2026 年 8 月 31 日全校提供 ChatGPT Edu；AI-Know 主要面向员工，学生可用指定职业辅助服务。工具开放不代表考核许可。
approved_tools.meaningEn: University teaching and learning; the course instructor’s assessment rules apply.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

research_publication.en: University-wide policy on AI use in research remains unverified/unknown from current official guidance. Specific domain guidance is established for publisher submissions and citation: submissions to NUS Press strictly forbid AI-generated text, polishing, and AI-generated images/diagrams, requiring detailed disclosure upon submission; NUS Libraries advises consulting specific publisher policies and style guides for research writing.
research_publication.zh: 全校研究规则仍有缺口；NUS Press 投稿禁止 AI 措辞、润色和生成图表并要求详细声明，这是出版范围，不是全校课程禁令。
research_publication.meaningEn: University teaching and learning; the course instructor’s assessment rules apply.
research_publication.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

academic_integrity.en: Submitting unacknowledged AI-generated work constitutes plagiarism and academic dishonesty under the Code of Student Conduct. AI detector verdicts are inadmissible as evidence in disciplinary processes or to penalize work (Section 2.6). Account sharing is strictly prohibited under any circumstances; using a shared account may raise collusion concerns and, where misconduct is established, may result in disciplinary action (Section 3).
academic_integrity.zh: 未注明 AI 作品构成诚信问题；检测判定不得作相关纪律证据或处罚依据。账号共享禁止，串通及处分须有成立依据。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Teaching staff, institutional services or disciplinary procedures as specified by the source; no extension to all student use.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

teaching_guidance.en: Prior approval is required through the AI System for Assurance and Evaluation before deploying AI to provide instruction, feedback, or marks (Section 2.4). Instructors should be transparent about AI deployment (Section 2.1). In general, except for AI marking of objective or closed-ended assessments, a human instructor or reviewer should remain in the loop. Spot checks should still be conducted even where AI scoring is considered reliable.
teaching_guidance.zh: AI 教学、反馈或评分须经指定系统事先审批；教师应透明使用，除客观闭合评分例外一般保留人工监督，并做抽检。
teaching_guidance.meaningEn: Teaching staff, institutional services or disciplinary procedures as specified by the source; no extension to all student use.
teaching_guidance.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

security_procurement.en: Educational deployment requires prior approval through the AI System for Assurance and Evaluation under the policy’s specified governance. ChatGPT Edu no-training protection is documented; approval for sensitive data and general procurement/security procedures remain unverified.
security_procurement.zh: 教学部署依指定治理审批；ChatGPT Edu 不训练承诺已有依据，但敏感数据及一般采购安全批准仍未核实。

clm-nus-ai-detectors-inadmissible.text: NUS policy states that verdicts of AI tools purporting to determine whether an input was generated by AI are not admissible as evidence in disciplinary processes to charge students with academic dishonesty or as justification to penalize student work.

evidence.quote:
The verdicts of current AI tools purporting to determine whether an analysed input has been
generated by AI are not admissible as evidence in a disciplinary process to charge a student
with academic dishonesty or as justification to penalize student work.

clm-nus-ai-marking-approval.text: NUS policy requires prior approval by Head of Department or Deanery under oversight of Chair of AI-COP, obtained via submission to the AI System for Assurance and Evaluation, before deploying AI to provide instruction, feedback, or marks. In general, except for AI marking of objective or closed-ended assessments, a human instructor or reviewer should remain in the loop, and spot checks should still be conducted even where scoring is considered reliable.

evidence.quote:
The use of AI tools to provide instruction to learners in the form of responses, feedback and/or
marks, whether as virtual tutors or as markers, requires prior approval by the Head of Department
or relevant Deanery, under the oversight of the Chair of the AI-COP. This is meant as due diligence
to balance innovation with ethical considerations. Institutional approval also shields the
individual instructors from complaints. Approval must be obtained through a submission to the
AI System for Assurance and Evaluation.

cc-ucl-25889d0c0278f271.text: The three categories are guidance for communicating assessment expectations. Assessment briefs take precedence; staff may specify additional conditions, and individual assistive-technology exemptions must be clarified.

evidence.quote:
For Category 1, you might use GenAI tools to help you revise and prepare, but the work you complete for the assessment should be your own.
In Category 2, you could use GenAI to get ideas, help draft your work, or even proofread what you've written. Just make sure you keep a note of how you've used GenAI, so that you can acknowledge it afterwards. You won't lose marks just for having used GenAI.
Category 3 is a lot like category 2, but there will also be some essential use of GenAI as part of the assessment.

clm-ucl-genai-acknowledgement-and-refere.text: UCL Library guidance requires acknowledgement where GenAI has functionally contributed to the creation of academic work (e.g. drafting, planning, structuring), subject to discipline and assessment instructions. Minimum acknowledgement includes tool name and version, publisher, URL, and single-sentence context of use. Prompts, generation dates, and tracked-changes are additional requirements that apply only when stipulated by departments or assignment briefs. Preparatory reading, search summaries, and basic grammar assistance may not require acknowledgement. While UCL advises treating AI output as a work with no author, students and researchers must follow required departmental guidelines and standardised referencing styles (such as APA or Chicago), which may require citing the GenAI tool as an author.

evidence.quote:
The use of GenAI must be acknowledged in any piece of academic work where it has been used as a functional tool to assist in the process of
creating
the academic work, such as drafting ideas and planning or structuring written materials.

clm-ucl-press-journals-editorial-policy-.text: UCL Press journals prohibit listing AI as an author on research-based works. Broadly, AI use in creating, editing, or manipulating images or figures is not accepted; however, an explicit exception permits AI-assisted technologies used as part of research design or methodology (e.g. data visualisation to generate or interpret underlying data), provided it is fully declared and documented in the methodology. Editors and peer reviewers are strictly prohibited from submitting manuscripts or data reported in them through AI tools.

evidence.quote: We therefore do not allow AI or LLM tools to be listed as an author on any research-based work published by UCL Press.
evidence.location: Continuous extracted-text characters 26278–26396; extracted text SHA256 479028ab551b3f540d23df04e812d201b205d0cb02509e255e18c46a02d612d4; raw source SHA256 3512c3c6e2292ab0d9df628f6ae43bc9b6516a8c6c75e0baad43cbc778280fdb; Lines 290–290; characters 26278–26396; excerpt offset 0–118

evidence.quote: Broadly, the use of AI-assisted technologies in the creation, editing, manipulating, enhancing, adjusting, obscuring, moving, removing or introducing any new specific feature within an image or figure, is not accepted.
evidence.location: Continuous extracted-text characters 27569–27787; extracted text SHA256 479028ab551b3f540d23df04e812d201b205d0cb02509e255e18c46a02d612d4; raw source SHA256 3512c3c6e2292ab0d9df628f6ae43bc9b6516a8c6c75e0baad43cbc778280fdb; Lines 295–295; characters 27569–27787; excerpt offset 0–218

evidence.quote: It would, however, be acceptable for AI-assisted technologies and tools that are used as part of research design or methodology (such as in AI-assisted imaging approaches to generate or interpret the underlying research data, for example in data visualisation), but this must be clearly declared as part of the methodology and full disclosure about what tools were used, how the tools were used, when this was used and explicably outline which images or figures were created using these tools. Where necessary, authors may be asked to provide pre-AI-adjusted versions of images and/or the composite raw images used to create the final submitted versions, for editorial assessment.

clm-ucl-teaching-grading-and-upload-rest.text: UCL does not invest in GenAI detection software. Staff must not submit student work into GenAI detection tools or GenAI services themselves, as this compromises students' intellectual property and personal data rights. Furthermore, due to lack of evidence that GenAI can mark effectively and without bias, staff should not use GenAI to mark student work. UCL markers do not use AI detector scores to establish academic misconduct. Initial informal discussions do not replace the formal Student Academic Misconduct Procedure; suspected inappropriate GenAI use or authorship issues may proceed through Stage 1 and an Investigatory Viva.

evidence.quote:
You may not use generative AI tools (e.g. ChatGPT, Copilot, Colab’s built-in AI) in this course.
This is not to deny the increasingly important role that LLMs play in the modern practice of programming and research; we merely note that, in an instructional capacity in an introductory course, we generally find them counterproductive.

The lone exception is that, on rare occasions, we may explicitly ask you to engage with AI tools on a per-problem basis.
These cases will be clearly marked on the respective homework sets.

clm-hku-assessment-instructor-instructio.text: HKU TALIC guidance requires teachers to clearly communicate acceptable AI use for course activities and assessed assignments. Instructors decide how to integrate AI; institutional tool access does not determine permission for a particular assessment.

evidence.quote: Teachers must be very clear in their guidance to students as to what is acceptable use of AI within the activities of their course and specifically on their assignments intended for assessment.
evidence.location: Transparency; public teaching guidance; normalized_extracted_text; quote characters 6696–6889; part 1/1.

clm-hku-law-ai-misuse-responses.text: For HKU Faculty of Law assessed work, an educative response may involve rewriting and resubmission with a penalty. Where this is not appropriate, an academic response may reduce the mark or give zero. Misuse may also be referred as a disciplinary offence; this is not automatic expulsion.

evidence.quote: When a teacher is satisfied that submitted work contains plagiarism or involves the misuse of generative and other AI tools, and that an educative response (usually involving re-writing and re-submission with a penalty) is not appropriate, then an academic response will be adopted, pursuant to which the plagiarized work may be given a mark of zero or a reduced mark. In addition, the matter may be treated as a disciplinary offence (just like the case of cheating during an examination) and referred to the University’s Disciplinary Committee under Statute XXXI of the University’s Statutes and the Disciplinary Committee Regulations.
evidence.location: Academic and disciplinary responses; normalized_extracted_text; quote characters 2805–3441; part 1/1.

clm-hku-law-permitted-ai-declaration.text: HKU Faculty of Law requires students to declare AI use on its assignment cover sheet where a teacher permits it for an assignment; failure to declare is treated as academic misconduct akin to plagiarism.

evidence.quote: In addition, the Faculty’s assignment cover sheet requires students to declare their use of AI tools, where this is permitted by a teacher for the purposes of an assignment. Failure to do so constitutes academic misconduct akin to plagiarism, and will be treated in the same manner.
evidence.location: Plagiarism and the Misuse of Generative and other AI tools in assessment; normalized_extracted_text; quote characters 2522–2804; part 1/1.

clm-hku-research-code-verification.text: HKU permits GenAI-generated research code only with documented and acknowledged use, verification of algorithms and software, and adequate testing that is conducted and reported.

evidence.quote: 23. Use of GenAI to generate computer code for research is only acceptable if a. the specific usage of the GenAI system is duly documented and acknowledged; b. the researcher has verified the correctness of the algorithm and software with respect to the intended use of the researcher; and c. the researcher conducts and reports adequate testing to ensure the software’s behaviours are well within user expectation.
evidence.location: Physical PDF page 4; section 23; dated 8 September 2025, Senate approval 23 September 2025.; raw_pdf_bytes; quote characters 10615–11030; part 1/1.

clm-hku-research-images-integrity.text: GenAI enhancement of research figures containing primary data is acceptable only if it does not alter interpretation. AI-generated images or other data should not be misrepresented as experimental data.

evidence.quote: 30. Use of GenAI tools to support image enhancement of figures that contain primary data is only acceptable if such modifications do not alter the interpretation of the data. 31. No AI-generated images and other data should be mis-represented as experimental data. F. Use of GenAI tools for peer reviewing research papers or funding applications
evidence.location: Physical PDF page 5; section 30–31; dated 8 September 2025, Senate approval 23 September 2025.; raw_pdf_bytes; quote characters 14332–14677; part 1/1.

clm-hku-research-peer-review-restriction.text: HKU does not accept use of GenAI in peer review of research outputs or funding applications because of integrity and confidentiality concerns.

evidence.quote: 32. The use of cloud-based commercial AI platforms has the potential to inadvertently disclose the content of papers or funding applications under review, thus violating the integrity and confidentiality of the established double-blind peer review process. Therefore, the use of GenAI in peer review of research output and funding applications is not acceptable.
evidence.location: Physical PDF page 5; section 32; dated 8 September 2025, Senate approval 23 September 2025.; raw_pdf_bytes; quote characters 14678–15040; part 1/1.

clm-ntu-ai-disclosure-submissions.text: NTU Library instructs students to disclose AI-tool use in their submissions and follow their module’s AI-use policy and instructor guidance. The required level of documentation and disclosure format depend on the assignment and instructor’s expectations; detailed prompt-and-output records and a particular declaration form are not universal requirements.

evidence.quote: Use AI tools to support tasks such as brainstorming, outlining, or checking grammar, but ensure you disclose their use in your submissions. Always refer to your module's AI use policy and seek guidance from your instructor regarding specific expectations for acceptable AI usage in your courses.
evidence.location: Key Points on Ethical AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 2828:3123

evidence.quote: When using AI for assignments (e.g., grammar checks, copyediting, or idea generation), adhere to the specific guidelines set by your instructor, as expectations may vary by module and discipline. This may include documenting your AI use, completing a “ Declaration on GAI Use ,” or disclosing AI contributions where required. To uphold academic integrity, you must always provide proper citations for all sources used, including AI‑generated content.
evidence.location: Purpose of Documenting, Disclosing and Citing AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 674:1124

clm-ntu-exam-external-resources-restrict.text: NTU Library instructs students not to access AI tools during examinations when external resources are not permitted. This condition does not establish either a ban in every exam or automatic AI permission in open-resource exams.

evidence.quote: Follow Exam Protocols. Do not access AI tools during examinations when external resources are not permitted to maintain fair testing conditions.
evidence.location: Consult, Follow Exam Protocols; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 722:866

clm-ntu-extensive-ai-instructor-permissi.text: NTU Library instructs students to obtain explicit instructor permission for more extensive AI involvement, such as generating source materials or enhancing visuals.

evidence.quote: Obtain explicit permission from your instructor for more extensive AI involvement, such as generating source materials or enhancing visuals.
evidence.location: Key Points on Ethical AI Usage; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 3124:3264

clm-ntu-genai-data-privacy.text: In research, confidential or sensitive information and personal data must not be uploaded to external GenAI platforms unless all applicable conditions are met: compliance with relevant laws and institutional policies; access restricted to authorised study members; no retention of the data in or by the GenAI; and, where applicable, explicit written permission from the data owner or agreement to that GenAI use in the Research Collaboration Agreement.

evidence.quote: Any confidential or sensitive information, and/or personal data must not be uploaded to any external GenAI software, system, or platform unless: The activity does not contravene any applicable laws, regulations, or institutional policies; Access to the GenAI is controlled and restricted to only authorised study members involved in the research; The data is not retained in or by the GenAI; and Where applicable, written permission has been explicitly provided by the data owner, or the use of such GenAI has been agreed upon in the Research Collaboration Agreement (RCA).
evidence.location: §4 Data Privacy & Confidentiality; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 6791:7364

clm-ntu-research-experimental-images.text: AI-generated research visuals must not be presented as actual experimental data unless AI or AI-assisted tools are an essential component of the research design and/or methodology. Using AI to fabricate images resembling experimental results constitutes serious research misconduct.

evidence.quote: AI-generated images, figures and videos must not be presented as actual experimental data unless AI (or AI-assisted) tools are an essential component of the research design and/or methodology. The use of AI to fabricate images to resemble experimental results constitutes serious research misconduct.
evidence.location: §3(ii); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5691:5991

clm-ntu-research-misconduct-referral.text: The Vice President (Research) reviews the RIO preliminary report and may take appropriate action, decide whether to invite the Provost to appoint a COI for faculty/research staff, or decide whether to refer a student to the Board of Discipline. This is a research-misconduct process, not an automatic AI penalty or a finding of guilt.

evidence.quote: 4.4.1 The Vice President (Research) shall review the preliminary investigation report from the RIO, who will then take appropriate action (especially in relation to research staff), or decide whether to invite the Provost to appoint a COI to consider the Allegation/ Complaint under the Framework for Investigation and Disciplinary Proceedings for Faculty and Research Staff, or if the Respondent is a student, decide whether to refer to the Board of Discipline, or take any other appropriate action.
evidence.location: Research misconduct procedures §4.4.1; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 15628:16128

clm-ntu-research-visual-labelling.text: NTU requires AI-generated research images, figures and videos to be clearly labelled and the methods, tools and parameters documented sufficiently for reproducibility.

evidence.quote: All AI-generated images, figures, and videos must be clearly labelled as such. Researchers are required to document the methods, tools, and parameters used to generate these visuals in sufficient detail to ensure reproducibility.
evidence.location: §3(i); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5457:5686

exams.en: There is no captured uniform exam permission. Law prohibits GenAI during exams by default unless the instructor specifies otherwise; BSD students should not rely on AI for exams without advance approval. Follow the exact unit and exam rules.

exams.meaningEn: Law and BSD rules are scoped; not a single University-wide ban.
exams.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

disclosure.en: Attribute AI assistance as required by student guidance and service/unit rules. PhoenixAI requires citation; Harris requires the specific tool citation and recommends saved outputs. Citation does not make prohibited Law work acceptable.
disclosure.zh: 按服务、课程及院系要求注明 AI；PhoenixAI 要求引用，Harris 要求工具引用并建议保留输出。引用不能使法学院禁用用途合法。
disclosure.meaningEn: Central student guidance, PhoenixAI terms and separate Harris/Law/BSD requirements.
disclosure.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

privacy_data.en: Confidential data requires prior review. Follow each tool’s data tier and narrower restrictions. Workspace Studio’s training opt-out warning and the general no-training rule both remain relevant; their reconciliation requires University clarification.
privacy_data.zh: 机密资料须事先审查，遵守具体工具数据等级；Workspace Studio 的训练退出提示与一般禁止训练规则并存，校方协调仍未核实。
privacy_data.meaningEn: University guidance and tool-specific restrictions; BSD and staff crosswalk scopes identified.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

approved_tools.en: The official table lists tools with data, purpose and procurement conditions. Student licence eligibility and vendor prices are not established by a table label; check the particular service and assessment rules.
approved_tools.zh: 目录仅列附数据、用途及采购条件的工具，不证明学生资格或价格；工具列入目录不构成考核授权。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Tool table review conditions, not universal student access or coursework approval.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

research_publication.en: Research data approval must cover the use. BSD scholarly work cannot name AI as an author; thesis/project use is subject to mentor or program discretion, scoped prior authorization and disclosure. Human research contributions remain the student’s own.
research_publication.zh: 批准须覆盖具体科研数据用途；BSD 不允许 AI 作者署名，论文或项目使用须依导师、项目或委员会裁量，保留个人核心研究并披露。

research_publication.meaningZh: 状态适用于下列来源列明的范围及条件；完整英文说明与原文保留如下。

academic_integrity.en: Instructor rules determine permitted use. College may use imperfect Pangram results as supporting information in a human-led process. College and Harris procedures differ; no automatic AI penalty is established.

academic_integrity.meaningZh: 仅适用于相应来源列明的对象、活动与条件；完整英文说明保留如下。

teaching_guidance.en: Student guidance directs students to instructor policies; Law deviations require a written syllabus. History’s default prohibits classroom GenAI absent a statement, and History faculty refrain from AI grading. BSD sample syllabus statements are examples, not universal policy.

security_procurement.en: Tools handling confidential data require review even when free. Paid tools use Procurement; free research/staff use has specified review conditions. A Risk Acceptance Letter may document agreed risks, not waive compliance prohibitions.

cc-uchicago-genai-guidance-1.text: Use of confidential data with publicly available GenAI tools is prohibited without prior security and privacy review. This includes personally identifiable employee, FERPA-covered student and HIPAA-covered patient data, and may include research that is not yet publicly available.

evidence.quote: The use of confidential data with publicly available generative AI tools is prohibited without prior security and privacy review. This includes personally identifiable employee data, FERPA-covered student data, HIPAA-covered patient data, and may include research that is not yet publicly available.
evidence.location: §1 Protection of University Data; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 1272:1571

clm-uchicago-area-administrative-resolut.text: Under the general Area process, where a student acknowledges responsibility and warning/probation is the likely outcome, the Dean may offer administrative resolution. The student may accept or reject in writing; acceptance is final and unreviewable within the University except if new material information leads to withdrawal and committee referral. This is not an automatic AI penalty.

evidence.quote: In situations where an individual student has acknowledged responsibility for misconduct and the most likely outcome for that misconduct would be a sanction of warning or disciplinary probation if the Area Disciplinary Committee were to be convened, the area Dean of Students (or designee) may offer to resolve the allegation of misconduct administratively without referral to an Area Disciplinary Committee. In such matters, the area Dean of Students can propose the sanction of an official warning or place the student on disciplinary probation for a specified period of time (e.g., a quarter, a year, for the duration of the student’s enrollment, etc.). The student will be
evidence.location: General Area administrative resolution; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 4646:5322

evidence.quote: given the option to accept or reject this offer for resolution in writing. If the student rejects this offer for resolution, then the area Dean of Students may refer the complaint to the Academic Dean with a recommendation to convene an Area Disciplinary Committee.
evidence.location: General Area administrative resolution; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 5323:5588

clm-uchicago-area-serious-sanction-autho.text: Under the general Area sanctions framework, only the Area Disciplinary Committee may suspend or expel a student; it may recommend revocation for misconduct before degree conferral. These are possible general sanctions, not fixed AI-use penalties or College-specific procedural deadlines.

evidence.quote: Only the Area Disciplinary Committee may impose a disciplinary suspension. During the period of suspension the student is barred from all University property, absent written permission from the Area Dean of Students, and is prohibited from exercising any rights and privileges of a student in the University. Unless the Area Disciplinary Committee specifically states otherwise in its decision, at the expiration of the period of suspension the student may resume active status as a student without any action on their part other than what would be required of any student who has, for a comparable period, interrupted their residence in the University for any other reason.
evidence.location: General Area sanctions, suspension/expulsion/degree revocation; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 23731:24405

evidence.quote: However, a student under suspension who has been charged with another offense may not resume active status as a student until final action has been taken on such charge by the Area Dean of Students or the Area Disciplinary Committee. The minimum length of a suspension is one full academic quarter. Disciplinary Expulsion Only the Area Disciplinary Committee may expel a student. A student who has been expelled is permanently excluded from all current and future academic programs. A student who has been expelled is barred from all University property, absent written permission from the Dean of Students in the University, and automatically forfeits all rights and privileges
evidence.location: General Area sanctions, suspension/expulsion/degree revocation; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 24406:25084

evidence.quote: as a student in the University and any degrees not actually conferred at the time of the expulsion. Revocation of the Degree The Area Disciplinary Committee may recommend revocation of the degree for misconduct that occurred before the degree was awarded.
evidence.location: General Area sanctions, suspension/expulsion/degree revocation; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 25085:25340

clm-uchicago-area-unit-procedure-boundar.text: Academic units have their own written disciplinary procedures; the central Area page provides a general outline. College students must use the separately published College process and Harris students must check Harris rules. General sanctions do not establish an automatic penalty for AI use.

evidence.quote: Each academic unit—the College, graduate divisions, professional schools, and the Graham School—has written procedures for student discipline. Those procedures may be obtained from the Office of the Dean of Students of the academic unit. General procedures for area discipline follow the outline of the procedures described below.
evidence.location: Area Disciplinary Systems, Unit-Specific Procedures; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 412:742

clm-uchicago-ccrf-ai-assisted-applicatio.text: CCRF prohibits materials prepared with generative AI assistance, expressly including Phoenix AI, in its undergraduate research and national fellowships applications.

evidence.quote: Because generative artificial intelligence technologies – including Claude, ChatGPT, Dall-E, Grammarly, and Phoenix AI – impede the independent pursuit of these core learning goals, submitting materials prepared with the aid of generative AI tools in CCRF’s undergraduate research and national fellowships applications is prohibited.
evidence.location: CCRF AI Policy; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 904:1237

clm-uchicago-college-disciplinary-standa.text: The College disciplinary process must not presume credibility or culpability. OCCS or the relevant committee gathers and evaluates information and determines responsibility by a preponderance of evidence. This is a general procedure, not an automatic AI penalty.

evidence.quote: The goal of the College disciplinary system is to ensure a fair and orderly process for fact gathering and decision-making regarding matters of possible student misconduct. In this undertaking, the OCCS, the Committee or the Subcommittee (as applicable) make no assumptions or presumptions, including about the credibility or culpability of the parties to the proceeding or witnesses. Neither the respondent nor the complainant bears the responsibility of proving or disproving allegations, and it is the role of OCCS, the Committee or Subcommittee (as applicable) to gather and/or evaluate information, apply an unbiased and transparent process, and determine by a preponderance
evidence.location: College Area Discipline Policy and Procedure, principles; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 2219:2898

evidence.quote: of the evidence whether the respondent violated our standards of conduct or a specific policy. Administrative and Formal Resolutions
evidence.location: College Area Discipline Policy and Procedure, principles; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 2899:3031

clm-uchicago-college-pangram-supporting-.text: College guidance recognises AI detectors are imperfect. Instructors and OCCS may use Pangram as supporting information in a transparent, human-led academic integrity process and student conversations; it is not automatic proof of misconduct. Unit policies and instructor choices may differ.

evidence.quote: AI detectors, including Pangram, are not perfect, though research from Booth faculty Brian Jabarian and Alex Imas indicates that Pangram is the best tool available (Jabarian & Imas, 2025). Accordingly, instructors and the Office of College Community Standards may use Pangram as one source of supporting information in a transparent, human-led academic integrity process and to guide conversations with students suspected of inappropriate AI use. OCCS is available to assist instructors in interpreting and weighing the results of a Pangram analysis.
evidence.location: AI Detection with Pangram; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 8435:8985

evidence.quote: Particular schools, divisions, and programs may have specific policies or guidance on whether or how to use Pangram. In some areas of the College, instructors have individual discretion to set the rules about AI use in their courses and to decide whether to use Pangram. Not all instructors will choose to use Pangram.
evidence.location: AI Detection with Pangram, unit scope; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 8116:8434

clm-uchicago-college-request-review.text: A College student may request review of a committee decision imposing a sanction after a responsibility finding. Review follows the separately referenced University procedures; no unverified deadline or automatic appeal outcome is inferred here.

evidence.quote: If the College Area Disciplinary Committee imposes a sanction following a finding of responsibility, the accused student may request to have the decision reviewed.
evidence.location: Requests for Review; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 26637:26800

clm-uchicago-college-review-response-rig.text: Before a College Area Disciplinary Committee meeting, the student receives the written materials and at least two business days to submit a response. This committee-stage rule must not be confused with other stages or academic units.

evidence.quote: The accused student will be informed in writing by OCCS of the referral and the date and time of the College Area Disciplinary Committee meeting where their case will be resolved. In advance of the meeting, the accused student will be provided with a copy of all written material furnished to the Area Disciplinary Committee and will be allowed at least two business days to complete and submit a response to OCCS prior to the matter being heard by the Area Disciplinary Committee.
evidence.location: Formal Resolution, materials and response; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 22064:22545

clm-uchicago-college-support-person.text: College students may bring a support person, who may advise but may not speak for the student or question the subcommittee. Students should notify OCCS three to five business days in advance; for a lawyer, notice should be at least seven business days and University counsel must also attend.

evidence.quote: Students may bring a person of their choice to any disciplinary-related meetings with the Dean of Students in the College or the Director of OCCS (or designee) or have them attend and provide support during phone calls or other interactions related to the investigation and resolution of an incident. The student can also be accompanied by their support person to any proceedings and during the subcommittee meeting (see below). The support person may confer quietly with the student during the proceedings and offer advice and other support during breaks. The support person may also assist with the review and preparation of materials, although authorship of statements should

evidence.quote: be the student’s alone. Support persons may not speak for the student during the proceedings and are not allowed to direct questions to the subcommittee members. If a support person violates the limitations regarding their role or engages in behavior or advocacy that harasses, abuses, or intimidates a witness, or an individual resolving the complaint, the support person may be required to leave the meeting or proceeding. Students should inform OCCS three to five business days before any proceedings if a support
evidence.location: College support persons and advance notice; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 10752:11429

evidence.quote: person will be attending. If the person providing support is a lawyer, a representative of the University’s Office of Legal Counsel must also attend the proceedings. The student should notify OCCS a minimum of seven business days before any proceedings the lawyer will be attending.

clm-uchicago-harris-disciplinary-probati.text: Harris disciplinary probation entails specified restrictions on emergency scholarship funding and Career Development/HarrisLink services, permanent ineligibility for on-campus academic jobs such as TA/proctor, and loss of good standing. Further violations during probation are referred to the Area committee. These are general sanction consequences, not automatic penalties for AI use.

Students who have been sanctioned with disciplinary probation are also permanently ineligible for on-campus academic jobs including teaching assistant (TA) and proctor. Students on disciplinary probation are not considered to be in good standing. Any additional violations of policy while on probation will be referred to the
evidence.location: Harris Disciplinary Process and Sanctions, updated 2 October 2026; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 49150:49829

evidence.quote: Area Disciplinary committee.

clm-uchicago-law-submitted-work-default.text: Under the Law School default, AI use in submitted work is compared to unattributed use of a human author’s work. Some uses such as brainstorming or proofreading can comply; AI composing all or part of a paper violates the default even with attribution.

evidence.quote: b) For all work that a student submits for any form of academic credit, AI may not be used, whether with or without attribution, in a way that would constitute academic plagiarism if the AI were a human author whose work was used without attribution . Commentary: The crux of this policy, which applies in any context in which a student submits work for evaluation, is the application of existing academic integrity policies. Thus, some but not all uses of AI in preparing work to submit for a class would violate this default policy. Using AI to brainstorm ideas for a paper—akin to asking a search engine (like Google), professors, or professional contacts for
evidence.location: Law §4.9(1)(b); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 7818:8480

evidence.quote: suggestions—would not violate this default policy. Nor would using AI for proofreading. The principle here is that if AI is performing a task that other technologies (or people) currently perform, and such uses are not a violation of academic integrity, then those uses of AI do not violate the default policy. In contrast, using AI to compose part or all of a paper, or copying or paraphrasing output from AI and passing it off as one’s own writing, would violate this default policy. The same principle applies here: if AI is performing a task that other technologies (or people) currently perform, and such uses are a violation of academic integrity, then those uses of AI do
evidence.location: Law §4.9(1)(b); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 8481:9159

evidence.quote: violate the default policy. The default policy sweeps more broadly than a prohibition against academic plagiarism, however. A student cannot avoid limits on the use of AI that would otherwise apply by attributing their work to AI. It is not plagiarism to copy or paraphrase another’s work, so long as one properly cites that source. But under the default policy, the use of AI with or without attribution is compared to the use of a human-created source without attribution . Thus, using AI to compose all or part of a paper, even if the use of generative AI is fully documented in properly placed footnotes , is a violation of the default policy.
evidence.location: Law §4.9(1)(b); normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 9160:9807

clm-uchicago-phoenix-citation.text: PhoenixAI users are responsible for citing generated content used in papers, presentations, course assignments or publications. Service access and citation do not override assessment restrictions.

evidence.quote: Users are responsible for properly citing the content generated by the service when it is used in academic papers, presentations, or any other form of course assignment or publication.
evidence.location: PhoenixAI Disclaimers, User Responsibility; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 4565:4749

clm-uchicago-student-coursework-guidance.text: UChicago student guidance requires students to follow the instructor’s rules on when and how AI may be used in coursework. Course policies may differ; students should ask when unclear.

evidence.quote: Always refer to the instructors’ guidance on when and how generative artificial intelligence may be used in course work. Instructors may opt to limit or otherwise specify when AI tools are and are not permitted. AI usage policies may vary from course to course. Always follow the instructors’ guidance and if you are unclear about what is allowed, please ask your instructor for clarification.
evidence.location: When Can I Use Generative AI to Support My Learning?; normalized extracted text; Unicode codepoints 1772:2165

academic_integrity.meaningEn: See source-specific course, academic unit and procedure conditions. Institution-wide audit remains PARTIAL.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 适用对象、院系和程序条件以下列完整来源为准；整校政策审计仍为 PARTIAL。

teaching_guidance.en: A teaching-centre report describes preliminary AI marking followed by teacher/TA review. This is a service workflow and reported practice, not a verified university-wide authorisation for autonomous final AI grading.
teaching_guidance.zh: 教学中心报道问学初步 AI 批改后由教师或助教复核；这是工作流程，不是全校自主 AI 最终评分授权。

security_procurement.en: Administrative-data safeguards have a specific institutional management scope. Final enactment of the model-security document titled 拟公开 remains unverified; no blanket student approval procedure is inferred.
security_procurement.zh: 校务数据管理规则有明确范围；标题含“拟公开”的模型安全文件最终生效状态未核实，不推定所有学生使用前须审批。

topicBasis.coursework: No university-wide AI coursework permission, prohibition or mandate was established. Institutional tool access and comparative policy classifications cannot supply that missing assessment rule.
topicBasis.exams: Undergraduate examinations restrict devices unless the chief examiner provides otherwise and require independent answers. These are general exam rules, not a verified uniform AI examination policy for every student.
topicBasis.disclosure: Declarations are required in the specified School of Integrated Circuits doctoral proposal and comprehensive-examination documents. No universal PKU AI declaration requirement is established; pre-defense wording and the revision chain retain explicit gaps.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Administrative-data systems have scoped security obligations; China Economic Quarterly referees must not upload confidential review material to public AI. These do not impose a uniform student AI registration procedure.
topicBasis.approved_tools: The official directory lists 33 distinct services/resources. Access for Wenxue, Xiaobei and the teacher-facing Doujiao announcement has specific conditions; other directory entries do not establish universal accounts or assessment permission.
topicBasis.research_publication: Explicit restrictions apply to named School of Integrated Circuits doctoral procedures and China Economic Quarterly referees. The Department of Information Management comparative resource is not treated as binding university-wide policy.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: General independent-work, attribution and misconduct procedures are distinguished from explicit School of Integrated Circuits AI restrictions. Findings and appropriate procedures are required; no automatic AI or detector-score penalty is established.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: A teaching-centre report describes preliminary AI marking followed by teacher/TA review. This is a service workflow and reported practice, not a verified university-wide authorisation for autonomous final AI grading.
topicBasis.security_procurement: Administrative-data safeguards have a specific institutional management scope. Final enactment of the model-security document titled 拟公开 remains unverified; no blanket student approval procedure is inferred.

do.en: Check the course and chief examiner’s instructions.
do.zh: 核对课程及主考教师的具体说明。

do.en: For IC doctoral proposals and comprehensive exams, make the required AI declaration.
do.zh: 集成电路学院博士开题和综合考试须按规定声明 AI 使用。

do.en: Use the correct disciplinary appeal or degree-review procedure.
do.zh: 区分纪律申诉与学位复核的适用程序。

dont.en: Do not treat tool access or comparative guidance as assessment permission.
dont.zh: 不要把工具开放或跨机构比较资料当作考核许可。

dont.en: In the specified IC doctoral procedures, do not generate core writing or fabricate data.
dont.zh: 集成电路学院指定博士环节不得 AI 生成核心论述或伪造数据。

dont.en: China Economic Quarterly referees must not upload confidential review material to public AI.
dont.zh: 《经济学》（季刊）审稿人不得把保密审稿材料上传公开 AI。

clm-pku-appeal-effect-and-external.text: Under the student appeal rules, the original decision continues during appeal, although the committee may recommend deferral where necessary. A student disagreeing with the review decision may appeal in writing to the Beijing education authority within 15 days after receiving the review conclusion or review decision. These are scoped general appeal rules.

evidence.quote:
第十二条
申诉处理期间相关处理或者处分决定不停止执行。学生申诉处理委员会认为必要的，可以建议学校暂缓执行有关决定。

第十五条
申诉人对学生申诉处理委员会的复查结论或学校相关机构的复查决定有异议的，可以在接到复查结论或复查决定之日起15日内，向北京市教育委员会提出书面申诉。

clm-pku-appeal-review-period.text: The student appeal committee must review and notify a conclusion within 15 days after the appeal is raised. In complex cases the period may be extended by 15 days with the president’s approval. This is the institution’s handling period, not the student’s appeal filing period.

evidence.quote:

学生申诉处理委员会应在申诉人提起申诉的日期起15日内对申诉进行复查，作出复查结论，并将复查结论告知申诉人。情况复杂不能在规定限期内做出结论的，经校长批准，可延长15日。

clm-pku-degree-academic-review.text: Under Article 34, a degree applicant may submit a written request to the department or degree subcommittee to review an academic evaluation (such as expert review, defense or achievement recognition). The University must reorganise expert review within 30 days after acceptance and notify the applicant in writing; that review decision is final. This is distinct from the student disciplinary appeal filing deadline.

AI use or a detector score alone is not established here as an automatic sanction.

clm-pku-disciplinary-appeal-filing.text: Within the scope of PKU’s student appeal rules, a student may submit a written appeal to the student appeal committee within 10 days after service of the relevant management or disciplinary decision. clm-pku-disciplinary-evidence-and-respon.text: PKU’s general student disciplinary rules require sufficient evidence, clear basis, accurate characterisation, proper procedure and proportionate sanctions. Before the department proposes action, students must be informed of the facts, reasons, basis and their right to make statements and defense. The rules apply to students in ordinary higher-degree education, not exclusively AI cases.

This applies to the specified school doctoral procedure, not every PKU assessment.
