topicBasis.exams: In University of Melbourne examinations, students must verify whether GenAI is authorised by the Subject Coordinator or exam instructions, and if permitted, use only approved tools and specified permitted uses. Tool access conveys no exam authorization, and unauthorised or undisclosed AI use in exams constitutes academic misconduct under MPF1310.
topicBasis.disclosure: University of Melbourne guidance mandates a dual disclosure framework: citing AI outputs in the reference list when quoting or paraphrasing does not replace an acknowledgement declaration; students must provide both a citation and a process declaration describing how tools were used, with unauthorised or undisclosed use constituting misconduct under MPF1310.
topicBasis.privacy_data: Students and researchers must not upload personal data, private information, third-party copyright, or patentable IP to external AI platforms. University teaching and assessment IP must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned environments; student LMS interactions and AILA session metadata are retained and reviewable by authorized decision-makers under the LMS privacy collection notice.
topicBasis.approved_tools: The University of Melbourne provides AILA within Canvas LMS where enabled by coordinators, SparkAI as a secure internal platform for staff (student access prohibited), Turnitin AI writing detection as an investigative diagnostic in similarity reports, and M365 Copilot Chat for student study support. Institutional access conveys neither coursework nor examination permission.
topicBasis.research_publication: Under section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) and active University guidance, researchers must document DAT use, disclose tools in outputs, and obtain privacy/security/ethics approvals. For graduate research theses, AI editing is strictly restricted to minor language and clarity support under Australian Standards for Editing Practice, with supervisor AI review requiring explicit written candidate consent.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Under MPF1310, unauthorised or undisclosed technology use in assessable work constitutes academic misconduct. Poor Academic Practice is managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, distinct from formal Faculty Level 1 and Serious Level 2 misconduct. Turnitin AI detection reports serve as an investigative prompt rather than proof, students have the right to provide drafts and explanations in exploratory discussions, and MPF1323 establishes a 20-university-business-day appeal window.
topicBasis.teaching_guidance: Melbourne teaching guidance advises Subject Coordinators to establish clear subject AI boundaries, model transparency, and provide guidance on translation and editing tool limits. GenAI tools must never substitute for staff evaluative judgement in marking or grading. Subjects are designed with at least 50% secure assessments to assure learning, supported by CSHE pedagogical assessment enhancement strategies.
topicBasis.security_procurement: The University of Melbourne AI Principles establish an overarching governance framework emphasizing fairness, literacy, privacy, and security; staff testing of assessment materials must remain within SparkAI or sanctioned environments rather than public third-party services.

do.en: Check your Subject Coordinator syllabus and specific examination instructions before using generative AI in exams or coursework.
do.zh: 在考试或学业成果中使用生成式 AI 前，仔细查验任课教师的大纲与具体考核要求。

do.en: Provide both a reference list citation when quoting/paraphrasing AI outputs and an acknowledgement declaration describing process assistance.
do.zh: 直接引用或转述 AI 输出时在参考文献中注明出处，并同时附具过程性使用声明说明工具使用环节。

do.en: Document digital assistance tool use, disclose tools in publications and theses, and obtain approvals under MPF1318 cl 5.11.
do.zh: 依据 MPF1318 第 5.11 条，记录数字辅助工具使用、在成果及论文中披露并取得隐私与伦理审批。

dont.en: Do not upload personal information, student records, confidential research, or third-party copyright materials to unauthorized public AI tools.
dont.zh: 切勿向未经授权的公开 AI 工具输入个人信息、学生记录、保密科研数据或第三方版权教学材料。

dont.en: Do not assume institutional tool access (AILA, SparkAI, M365 Copilot Chat) conveys permission for course assignments or examinations.
dont.zh: 切勿将学校开通某款 AI 工具（如 AILA、SparkAI、Copilot Chat）等同于获准将其用于课程作业或考试。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI tools in examinations or assessable work without Subject Coordinator authorization or disclosure, which constitutes academic misconduct under MPF1310.
dont.zh: 切勿在未获任课教师明确许可或未加披露的情况下在考试或学业成果中使用生成式 AI 工具，否则构成 MPF1310 学术不端。

claim-university-of-melbourne-5.text: At the University of Melbourne, using GenAI tools on an assessment task that does not permit them, or using them in preparation without acknowledgement, constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).
claim-university-of-melbourne-5.scope: Student academic integrity and disciplinary procedures

evidence.quote: It’s important your students realise that if an assessment task does not permit the use of such tools, or if they use such tools in the preparation of an assessment submission without acknowledgement, this constitutes academic misconduct under cl. 4.13 of the Student Academic Integrity Policy (MPF1310).
evidence.location: Section: University policies in relation to Generative AI; extracted text lines 57-57

claim-university-of-melbourne-10.text: A high AI score in Turnitin's writing detection report is not proof of misconduct and does not on its own constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.
claim-university-of-melbourne-10.scope: Turnitin AI score interpretation and misconduct threshold

evidence.quote: A high AI score in Turnitin’s writing detection report is not proof that academic misconduct has taken place (any more than would be the case when using the more familiar similarity report tool to flag potential plagiarism).  It does not, on its own, constitute grounds for making an allegation of academic misconduct.
evidence.location: Section: Turnitin Writing Detection Guidance; extracted text lines 37-37

cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.text: AILA is listed for The University of Melbourne in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: self_hosted_system.
cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.scope: Canvas LMS student chatbot developed by Product Innovation Team

evidence.quote: The University’s Product Innovation Team has developed the AI learning assistant (AILA): a chatbot embedded in the LMS and intended as a learning resource for students.
evidence.location: Section: AI Learning Assistant (AILA); extracted text lines 80-80

cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.text: SparkAI is listed for The University of Melbourne in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: self_hosted_system.
cl-the-university-of-melbourne-instituti.scope: Secure internal staff platform (spark.unimelb.edu.au); student access prohibited

evidence.quote: SparkAI is a secure platform internal to the University of Melbourne that can be accessed by staff (but not by students). It allows staff to explore Generative AI tools and capabilities using information that may be sensitive to the University, such as teaching/assignment materials, potentially copyrighted material, or other data that have Intellectual Property overlays.
evidence.location: Section: SparkAI Platform; extracted text lines 67-67

cl-the-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-.text: Turnitin AI writing detection is listed for The University of Melbourne in an official university AI tools source. Derived availability: conditionally allowed. Derived endorsement type: institutionally_licensed_or_procured.
cl-the-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-.scope: Canvas similarity report staff diagnostic (not a student generative tool)

evidence.quote: Turnitin’s AI writing detection tool is currently accessible to staff within Canvas as part of its similarity report function, for work submitted in English.
evidence.location: Section: Turnitin AI Detection; extracted text lines 32-32

claim-university-of-melbourne-1.text: Before using GenAI for assessment-related work, University of Melbourne students must check that their Subject Coordinator has authorised its use.

evidence.quote: Before you use GenAI for assessment-related work you must check to ensure that your Subject Coordinator has authorised its use.
evidence.location: Section: Is it okay to use GenAI at Melbourne?; extracted text lines 6-6

claim-university-of-melbourne-11.text: Because third-party external platforms such as ChatGPT use prompts and inputs to further train their models, University of Melbourne staff must not enter assessments, teaching materials, or sensitive IP into third-party platforms, reserving such testing for SparkAI or sanctioned platforms.
claim-university-of-melbourne-11.scope: External platform data retention and teaching IP protection

evidence.quote: Since assessments and other teaching materials constitute University IP, they should never be tested on third-party external platforms such as ChatGPT, since these platforms use all prompts and inputs to further train their models.  Any such testing/auditing must be done only within the University’s secure GenAI platform (SparkAI) or other University of Melbourne-sanctioned platforms.
evidence.location: Section: Data Privacy and AI Training Risks; extracted text lines 41-41

claim-university-of-melbourne-12.text: If students use an AI tool such as ChatGPT to generate output that is paraphrased or directly quoted in assessable writing, it must be cited and referenced as a source in the reference list.
claim-university-of-melbourne-12.scope: Assessment citation and reference list formatting

evidence.quote: If you have used an AI tool or technology such as ChatGPT to generate an output which you either paraphrase or direct quote in your writing, you must cite and reference this output as a source in your reference list.
evidence.location: Section: Citing AI Output in Reference List; extracted text lines 15-15

claim-university-of-melbourne-15.text: Generative AI tools can only be used in research outputs if material generated or substantially altered is acknowledged according to University policy and the Australian Code for the Responsible Conduct of Research.
claim-university-of-melbourne-15.scope: Research publication and Code for Responsible Conduct

evidence.quote:
This clarifies
that generative AI tools can only be used if material that is generated or substantially altered by these tools is
acknowledged according to the University’s policy and the Australian Code for the Responsible Conduct of Research.
evidence.location: Section: Inquiry Submission - Research Conduct; extracted text lines 229-231

claim-university-of-melbourne-16.text: Researchers are advised not to share confidential information or innovation details in generative AI prompts, as that may cause IP to no longer be owned by the researcher or University.
claim-university-of-melbourne-16.scope: Research confidentiality, data, and patentable inventions

evidence.quote:
The University has advised researchers that they should
not share confidential information or information about an innovation  in a generative AI prompt, as that may mean
that the IP is no longer owned by the researcher or by the University.
evidence.location: Section: Inquiry Submission - Commercial IP and Confidentiality; extracted text lines 252-254

claim-university-of-melbourne-2.text: University of Melbourne students must protect personal information and not upload full names, dates of birth, addresses, or other confidential, sensitive or private information to GenAI tools.

evidence.quote: Protect your personal information and that of others. Do not upload your full name, date of birth, address or other confidential, sensitive or private information.
evidence.location: Section: Protecting Personal Information; extracted text lines 44-44

claim-university-of-melbourne-3.text: When uploading material to an AI tool, University of Melbourne students must ensure they do not violate creator copyright without permission.

evidence.quote: When you upload this material to an AI tool, you may be violating the copyright of creators who have not given permission to do this with their material.
evidence.location: Section: Respecting Copyright; extracted text lines 47-47

claim-university-of-melbourne-6.text: Each University of Melbourne subject coordinator is responsible for setting out the bounds of appropriate GenAI use within their subject and having conversations with students for clarity.

evidence.quote: It follows that it is the responsibility of each subject coordinator to set out the bounds of appropriate GenAI use within their subject. Coordinators are strongly encouraged to consider possible use case scenarios for their assessments, set clear boundaries, and have conversations with their students to enable clarity about what tools are appropriate and for what tasks.
evidence.location: Section: Setting Subject Boundaries; extracted text lines 58-58

claim-university-of-melbourne-7.text: Assessments and teaching materials constitute University IP and must never be tested on third-party external platforms like ChatGPT; testing or auditing must be done only within SparkAI or sanctioned platforms.
claim-university-of-melbourne-7.scope: Staff materials review and institutional IP

evidence.quote: Since assessments and other teaching materials constitute University IP, they should never be tested on third-party external platforms such as ChatGPT, since these platforms use all prompts and inputs to further train their models.  Any such testing/auditing must be done only within the University’s secure GenAI platform (SparkAI) or other University of Melbourne-sanctioned platforms.
evidence.location: Section: Protecting University Intellectual Property; extracted text lines 41-41

claim-university-of-melbourne-9.text: At the University of Melbourne, use of GenAI tools for marking or grading should never be a substitute for staff exercising their own evaluative judgement.
claim-university-of-melbourne-9.scope: Staff evaluative judgment and AI-assisted marking limits

evidence.quote: Use of GenAI tools should never be a substitute for staff exercising their own evaluative judgement.
evidence.location: Section: University policies in relation to Generative AI, subsection: Can staff use GenAI for marking/grading of student work?; extracted text lines 63-63

claim-university-of-melbourne-8.text: University of Melbourne staff may use GenAI tools to help prepare teaching materials provided care is exercised for proper use of University IP and ethical AI use.

evidence.quote: Staff can use GenAI tools to help in the preparation of teaching materials, however care must always be exercised to ensure proper use of university IP, and ethical use of GenAI.
evidence.location: Section: Staff Teaching Materials Preparation; extracted text lines 61-61

claim-university-of-melbourne-13.text: University of Melbourne staff should consider and provide advice on the limits of acceptable use of AI-powered translation and editing tools (e.g. Grammarly, Google Translate) in their subjects, as student use can extend to the point where students are no longer expressing their own ideas.
claim-university-of-melbourne-13.scope: Staff subject guidance on AI translation and editing boundaries

evidence.quote: Student use of these tools may pose risks to academic integrity, and staff should consider and provide advice on the limits of acceptable use in their subject. Use of these tools can easily extend to the point where students are no longer expressing their own ideas or understanding of the subject matter.
evidence.location: Section: AI and assessment, subsection: Is it okay if students use GenAI for language translation or editing their work?; extracted text lines 51-51

claim-university-of-melbourne-17.text: In its 2023 submission, the University encouraged optional government sector guidance and communities of practice to share best practice in GenAI education.
claim-university-of-melbourne-17.scope: Sector policy recommendations and communities of practice

evidence.quote:
Government may wish to develop optional guidance on the use of generative AI in the sector. The
Government could also establish communities of practice to share ideas , best practice and lessons learned in
generative AI in higher education.
evidence.location: Section: Inquiry Submission - Recommendations; extracted text lines 45-47

claim-university-of-melbourne-18.text: The Faculty of Architecture, Building and Planning (BEL+T) provides discipline-specific guidance offering educators key concepts and definitions for generative AI in built environments.
claim-university-of-melbourne-18.scope: Faculty disciplinary guidance in architecture and built environments

evidence.quote: This BEL+T Guidance on Generative AI (genAI) offers ABP subject coordinators, and other educators in built environments disciplines, some key concepts and definitions in this fast-developing space.
evidence.location: Section: BEL+T Guidance Scope; extracted text lines 4-4

claim-university-of-melbourne-4.text: At the University of Melbourne, students are expected to produce their own perspective, experience, and knowledge in assessable work rather than rely on AI output alone.

evidence.quote: While GenAI can produce seemingly valuable or original output, your own perspective, experience and knowledge is what the University and future employers expect. Therefore, knowing what value you add is crucial.
evidence.location: Section: Demonstrating Your Knowledge; extracted text lines 60-60

claim-university-of-melbourne-14.text: Specific guidance for University of Melbourne researchers regarding acknowledging digital assistance tools in research outputs is available via the Research Ethics and Integrity website.
claim-university-of-melbourne-14.scope: Research ethics and digital assistance tool guidance

evidence.quote: Researchers: Specific guidance for University of Melbourne researchers about how to acknowledge the use of digital assistance tools in research outputs is available at the Research ethics and integrity website.
evidence.location: Section: Guidance for Researchers; extracted text lines 8-8

claim-university-of-melbourne-citation-v.text: University of Melbourne guidance mandates that citing AI outputs in the reference list does not replace an acknowledgement declaration: students who cite or paraphrase AI outputs must still provide a declaration detailing how AI tools were used across the assessment process.
claim-university-of-melbourne-citation-v.scope: Dual requirement of citation and declaration for assessment submissions

evidence.quote:
I have cited and referenced outputs from an AI tool or technology in my assessment. Do I also need a declaration?
Yes. In addition to a citation or reference, a declaration provides you with an opportunity to describe how you have used an AI tool or technology to complete your assessment. This information assists your readers to understand how AI tools and technologies have been incorporated in your research, writing and learning processes.
evidence.location: Section: Acknowledging AI Tools (Declaration Requirement FAQ); extracted text lines 59-60

claim-university-of-melbourne-student-ex.text: In University of Melbourne examinations, students must verify whether GenAI use is authorised for the specific exam, and if permitted, ensure that only approved tools and specified uses are employed in alignment with University policy.
claim-university-of-melbourne-student-ex.scope: Student examination conduct and open-book exam rules

evidence.quote: Make sure you know whether the use of GenAI tools is authorised in the exam, and if so, which tools or specific uses are allowed
evidence.location: Section: Open-book exams advice - GenAI authorization check; extracted text lines 58-58

evidence.quote: If you use GenAI tools to assist in preparing or completing your exam, it is your responsibility to do so ethically, responsibly and in alignment with University of Melbourne policy.
evidence.location: Section: Open-book exams advice - Ethical responsibility; extracted text lines 60-60

claim-university-of-melbourne-exam-rules.text: Under University guidelines on assuring learning in the age of GenAI, in most cases subjects are designed so that secure assessment types account for at least 50% of total marks, with phased implementation (2026–2028) and programmatic exceptions.
claim-university-of-melbourne-exam-rules.scope: Assuring learning guidelines and secure assessment curriculum design

evidence.quote:
In most cases, this means designing subjects so that “secure” assessments, in which learning
is assured, account for at least 50% of a subject’s mark (Principle 1).
evidence.location: Section: Assuring Learning Guidelines Principle 1; extracted text lines 10-11

claim-university-of-melbourne-technology.text: The University of Melbourne academic misconduct framework explicitly categorizes unauthorized or undisclosed use of technology (including GenAI) as a breach type under academic integrity procedures.
claim-university-of-melbourne-technology.scope: Student Academic Integrity Policy breach categories

evidence.quote:
Breach types
Plagiarism
Unauthorised re-use of previous work (self plagiarism)
Breach of examination or assessment rules or directions
Falsification or misrepresentation of data
Unauthorised or undisclosed use of technology (incl. GenAI)
evidence.location: Section: Managing Suspected Academic Misconduct - Breach Types; extracted text lines 128-133

claim-university-of-melbourne-misconduct.text: Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures managed educatively by Subject Coordinators, and is explicitly distinct from academic misconduct.
claim-university-of-melbourne-misconduct.scope: Student Academic Integrity Policy procedural classifications

evidence.quote:
Poor academic practice refers to minor and unintentional departures from accepted scholarly conventions or failures to comply with assessment guidelines. Poor academic practice incidents are characterised by inexperience, lack of student knowledge, or poor academic skills, and does not compromise the purpose and/or integrity of the assessment.
Importantly, poor academic practice is not academic misconduct, may be treated as an assessment matter and managed within the marking and assessment guidelines set by the Board of Examiners for the subject.
evidence.location: Section: Poor Academic Practice Definition and Management; extracted text lines 66-67

claim-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-i.text: Turnitin AI detection results serve only as a prompt for further investigation; if suspected, students may be invited to explain their work and provide drafts or notes in an exploratory discussion.
claim-university-of-melbourne-turnitin-i.scope: Turnitin AI investigative procedures and student rights

evidence.quote:
As with the similarity report generated by Turnitin, the result of the AI writing detector tool is a prompt for further investigation.
Should there be a suspicion that part or all of your submitted assessment has been produced using generative AI, you may be asked to explain your essay and argument (how you developed the argument, what sources you used, how you reached the conclusion you did), or to provide drafts or notes of early versions of the assessment.
evidence.location: Section: Advice for Students Regarding Turnitin - Prompt for investigation; extracted text lines 15-16

claim-university-of-melbourne-appeals-wi.text: Under University of Melbourne student appeals procedures, appeals against academic misconduct decisions must be submitted via the online form within 20 University business days from the original decision date.

evidence.quote: To submit an appeal, you must complete the online student appeals form within 20 University business days from the date of the original decision.
evidence.location: Section: Submitting an Appeal - 20 Business Days Window; extracted text lines 126-126

claim-university-of-melbourne-copilot-ch.text: University of Melbourne students have access to M365 Copilot Chat with their student account, supporting study with private OneDrive data protection; assessment use must follow subject rules and be properly acknowledged.

evidence.quote: M365 Copilot Chat provides a secure, AI-powered chat experience grounded in web knowledge and powered by GPT. While students are allowed to use GenAI for study, all work submitted for assessment must follow the rules of the assessment and, if AI use is permitted, students must ensure this is acknowledged as described in Academic Integrity: unauthorised or undisclosed use of technology.
evidence.location: Section: M365 Copilot Chat - Overview and study rules; extracted text lines 162-162

claim-university-of-melbourne-research-i.text: Under section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) and University guidance, research personnel must document digital assistance tool use, disclose DAT use to collaborators and in outputs (including theses), and obtain all required privacy, security, and ethics approvals.
claim-university-of-melbourne-research-i.scope: Responsible Conduct of Research Policy (MPF1318) section 5.11 obligations

evidence.quote:
In line with section 5.11 of the Responsible Conduct of Research Policy, research personnel are responsible for assuring the integrity of their research produced with the assistance of digital assistance tools, including but not limited to artificial intelligence (AI) tools. Research personnel must:
Document the use of a digital assistance tool (DAT) in their research process
Disclose the use of a DAT to research partners, collaborators and in research outputs, including but not limited to publications and theses
evidence.location: Section: Responsible Conduct of Research Policy cl. 5.11 obligations; extracted text lines 36-38

evidence.quote: Ensure all necessary approvals are obtained to use the DAT, including but not limited to a Privacy Impact Assessment, Information Security Risk Assessment, or ethical review and approval where applicable.
evidence.location: Section: Approvals for DAT Use; extracted text lines 39-39

claim-university-of-melbourne-graduate-t.text: For graduate researchers and research theses, digital assistance and GenAI use is strictly limited to minor editorial support (language, clarity, spelling, grammar) under the Australian Standards for Editing Practice; substantial redrafting is prohibited and supervisor AI review requires explicit written permission.
claim-university-of-melbourne-graduate-t.scope: Graduate research thesis editing standards and supervisor AI consent

evidence.quote: Whether rephrasing text moves beyond minor editing assistance, and therefore impacts the integrity of the research output, depends on whether the rephrasing is beyond that acceptable according to the Australian Standards for Editing Practice. These standards limit editing to language and expression (clarity, grammar, spelling), completeness and consistency. Substantial redrafting of whole paragraphs or larger sections, or translating a substantial body of text into English, falls outside those limits.
evidence.location: Section: Australian Standards for Editing Practice and thesis limits; extracted text lines 84-84

evidence.quote:
A specific case is material provided to supervisors by their graduate researchers. These candidates own their text so it can only be uploaded into an AI with their explicit permission and with a clear statement of the purpose for which it is being uploaded. This also applies to co-authored material such as drafts of papers.
Thus, if a supervisor plans to use AI to provide feedback on written material, they must obtain the candidate’s permission to do so, and it is a reasonable expectation on the part of the candidate that this permission be recorded in writing.
evidence.location: Section: Supervisor AI Review Permission; extracted text lines 80-81

claim-university-of-melbourne-aila-lms-p.text: Student interactions with LMS-embedded tools such as AILA are governed by the University LMS privacy collection notice: interaction metadata, assessment content, and system records are retained in the LMS and may be reviewed to verify authorship or investigate suspected policy breaches, accessible to authorized decision-makers.
claim-university-of-melbourne-aila-lms-p.scope: LMS data logging, AILA conversation retention, and misconduct investigation access

evidence.quote: Assessment content, metadata and system activity records may be reviewed where necessary to verify authorship, ensure fair assessment conditions, or investigate suspected breaches of University’s policies.
evidence.location: Section: LMS Privacy Collection Notice - Assessment records and review; extracted text lines 22-22

evidence.quote:
Your personal information may be disclosed to:
Visiting or honorary academics involved in teaching and grading
Decision-makers involved in academic integrity or misconduct processes
Service providers including Learning and Management System provider (Instructure Inc) and other integrated educational technologies
evidence.location: Section: LMS Privacy Collection Notice - Disclosure to Decision-makers; extracted text lines 30-33

claim-university-of-melbourne-cshe-asses.text: The Melbourne CSHE provides a range of pedagogical strategies for using GenAI tools to enhance assessment tasks.
claim-university-of-melbourne-cshe-asses.scope: Assessment design and CSHE pedagogical guidance

evidence.quote: The CSHE website includes a range of strategies for using GenAI tools to enhance assessment tasks.
evidence.location: Section: Enhancing Assessment Tasks; extracted text lines 47-47

claim-university-of-melbourne-secure-vs-.text: Assuring student learning requires careful use of secure assessment types at key points where student authorship can be verified, contrasted with open assessments where rules may be circumvented.

evidence.quote: Assuring student learning requires the careful use of ‘secure’ assessment types at key points in the curriculum. Secure assessment types are those for which we can have high confidence that assessment rules were followed and can verify that the student completed the task. This is in contrast to ‘open’ assessments where rules may be more easily circumvented.
evidence.location: Section: Assuring Learning at Melbourne; extracted text lines 3-3

claim-university-of-melbourne-ten-ai-pri.text: The University of Melbourne AI Principles commit to building awareness among students and staff of their responsibilities around AI tools in work preparation and managing integrity-related risks.

evidence.quote: The University of Melbourne will build awareness among students and staff of their responsibilities around the use of AI tools in the preparation of work and we will manage integrity-related risks posed by AI tools.
evidence.location: Section: University of Melbourne AI Principles - Academic and Research Integrity; extracted text lines 8-8

unsw-sydney.name: University of New South Wales (UNSW Sydney)

scope.en: Student Plagiarism Management Procedure; Assessment and Feedback Procedure; Information Governance Procedure; Library TDM Guidance. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 学生抄袭管理程序、考核与反馈程序、信息治理程序及图书馆 TDM 指引。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: Assessment tasks follow transitional period frameworks: six Levels of AI Assistance (No Assistance, Simple Editing Assistance, Planning or Design Assistance, Assistance with Attribution, Generative AI Software-based Assessments, Not Applicable) apply to Term 3 2026, Semester 2 2026, and Hexamester 5 2026; three AI Assessment Modes (Can't Use AI, Can Use AI, Must Use AI) apply to Hexamester 6 2026 and Summer Term 2027. Unless stated otherwise, the Assessment and Feedback Procedure applies from Term 3 2026, Semester 2 2026, and Hexamester 1 2027. Clauses 1.1–1.2 and 1.4 apply from 1 January 2027; clauses 2.1–2.2 and 3.5–3.7 apply from 1 January 2028. Current assessments must follow the instructions for the relevant teaching period and course.
coursework.zh: 课程考核遵循各学期的具体过渡框架：2026年第3学期、第2半学年及第5六分学期适用六级 AI 辅助框架（禁止辅助、简易编辑辅助、规划设计辅助、归属引用辅助、基于生成式 AI 软件的考核、不适用）；2026年第6六分学期及2027年夏季学期适用三种 AI 考核模式（不可使用、可以使用、必须使用）。除另有说明外，《考核与反馈程序》自 2026 年第 3 学期、2026 年第 2 半学年及 2027 年第 1 六分学期起适用。第 1.1–1.2 及 1.4 条自 2027 年 1 月 1 日起适用；第 2.1–2.2 及 3.5–3.7 条自 2028 年 1 月 1 日起适用。具体考核仍须遵循所属学期和课程的具体指引。
coursework.meaningEn: Student Plagiarism Management Procedure; Assessment and Feedback Procedure; Information Governance Procedure; Library TDM Guidance. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
coursework.meaningZh: 学生抄袭管理程序、考核与反馈程序、信息治理程序及图书馆 TDM 指引。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

exams.en: Assessments designated 'No Assistance' or 'Can't Use AI' prohibit generative AI use. Follow the framework and instructions for the relevant teaching period; suspected misuse is handled under the applicable academic integrity procedure.
exams.zh: 标明 No Assistance 或 Can't Use AI 的考核禁止使用生成式 AI。请遵守所属学期的框架及考核要求；涉嫌违规的情况依适用学术诚信程序处理。
exams.meaningEn: Student Plagiarism Management Procedure; Assessment and Feedback Procedure; Information Governance Procedure; Library TDM Guidance. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
exams.meaningZh: 学生抄袭管理程序、考核与反馈程序、信息治理程序及图书馆 TDM 指引。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

privacy_data.en: UNSW's Information Governance Policy applies to students, researchers, research trainees, employees and affiliates; individual procedures may have narrower scope. Student guidance separately advises against including personal or sensitive information in AI prompts.

academic_integrity.en: UNSW manages academic integrity under the Student Plagiarism Management Procedure across five tiers: Poor scholarship, Minor, Moderate, Significant, and Serious. For Minor plagiarism, the rubric states that a mark reduction should not exceed 10% of the maximum grade available for the assessment task (from plagiarism rubric Appendix 3 footnote 4, not an absolute cap). School authorities manage Poor scholarship and Minor through Significant cases. Serious cases must be referred to the Conduct & Integrity Office (CIO) as potential student misconduct, with potential outcomes ranging from task/course failure to suspension or exclusion (not automatic penalties). Actions outside the outcomes available for a level require CIO approval, and repeated instances may also be escalated to student misconduct. For School-level outcomes notified under clause 4.3(a), an internal review request must be made within 20 business days of that notice and is limited to procedural fairness, not the merits. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process.
academic_integrity.zh: UNSW 依据《学生抄袭管理程序》将学术不端划分为五个层级：学术素养不足（Poor scholarship）、轻微（Minor）、中度（Moderate）、重大（Significant）及严重（Serious）。对于 Minor 抄袭，细则明确规定扣分应不超过该项评估最高可得分的 10%（源自抄袭细则附录 3 脚注 4，并非法定硬性上限）。学院负责处理轻微至重大层级的案例；严重案例移交品行与诚信办公室（CIO）按可能构成学生不端行为处理，处理措施（包括不及格、停学或除名）属可能裁定而非自动适用。超出对应层级可用结果的处理需经 CIO 批准，重复违规亦可转为不当行为程序。对于依据第 4.3(a) 条通知的学院层级处理结果，内部复核须在收到该通知后 20 个工作日内提出，范围限于程序公平而非处理结论本身；Serious 案件另走 CIO 程序。

do.en: Check the AI framework for your teaching period and each assessment: six Levels apply to Term 3, Semester 2 and Hexamester 5 in 2026; three Modes apply to Hexamester 6 in 2026 and Summer Term 2027.

do.en: Provide clear acknowledgement and referencing when generative AI tools are permitted and used in assessable tasks.

do.en: For School-level outcomes under clause 4.3(a), email a procedural-fairness review request to the Head of School or delegate within 20 business days of the outcome notice. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process.

dont.en: Do not use generative AI in assessments marked 'No Assistance' or 'Can't Use AI'; follow the relevant teaching-period framework and assessment instructions.
dont.zh: 切勿在标明 No Assistance 或 Can't Use AI 的考核中使用生成式 AI；请遵守所属学期框架及具体考核要求。

dont.en: Where the UNSW AI governance procedure applies, do not use AI without the required self-assurance assessment; approved, deployed enterprise-grade systems such as Copilot are exempt. Maintain confidentiality of highly sensitive, sensitive, commercial and personal information.

dont.en: Do not assume institutional rollout (such as Copilot or ChatGPT Edu) conveys blanket permission for course assignments or examinations.

claim-unsw-sydney-17.text: UNSW's teacher guidance describes preliminary checks and consultation for suspected AI writing. Under the formal Student Plagiarism Management Procedure, the Course Authority or SSIA should notify the student in writing of detected Poor scholarship/Minor/Moderate/Significant plagiarism and proposed academic action; the student has 5 business days to respond. For these School-level outcomes, an internal review must be emailed to the Head of School or delegate within 20 business days of the Notification of Outcome under clause 4.3(a). Review is limited to procedural fairness, not the merits. The reviewer must not have participated in the initial decision; the student is to be notified of the review outcome within 10 business days of receipt of the review request. Serious cases follow the separate CIO process; these School-level deadlines must not be presented as deadlines for every serious-misconduct case.

Follow the service's access restrictions and applicable data agreements; these classifications do not settle authorization for every dataset.

academic_integrity.en: Inserting AI-generated content into submitted work without proper attribution constitutes an academic integrity violation. Under GSAS 2026–2027 standards, graduate students must consult relevant faculty before using AI in coursework or research and must be prepared to articulate and demonstrate their drafting process if requested, but there is no universal requirement for all students to log every prompt. Disciplinary responses are managed by the Committee on Regulations and Discipline; written student statements are ordinarily due within two weeks.

draft-claim-yale-gsas-writing-process-dr.text: Under GSAS 2026–2027 standards, graduate students have the responsibility to be able to articulate explicitly the process by which they conduct research and draft work, including the ability to provide a draft history of submitted work demonstrating original thought and composition. In evaluating disciplinary allegations involving inappropriate use of AI tools, the absence of this material or an inability to articulate clearly the research and writing process may be taken into account.

evidence.quote: Additionally, graduate students have the responsibility to be able to articulate explicitly the process by which they conduct research and draft work, including the ability to provide a draft history of any work submitted for evaluation that demonstrates original thought and composition. The absence of this material and/or the inability to articulate clearly the research and writing process may be taken into account in evaluating disciplinary allegations involving inappropriate use of AI tools.
evidence.location: lines 177-177; Research and drafting process articulation and draft history

draft-claim-yale-gsas-discipline-committ.text: Under GSAS Committee on Regulations and Discipline procedures, students are asked to respond in writing to an allegation ordinarily within two weeks. Hearings are conducted by a panel of at least four members (including a usually non-voting secretary; three voting members including at least one student form a quorum). Decisions are made by secret ballot on a preponderance of the evidence; the committee recommends a sanction to the dean, who determines the penalty. Disciplinary decisions take immediate effect. Students may submit a written appeal to the Committee of Review no later than five business days after the committee decision. The Committee of Review (three members) may decline action or request reconsideration; on reconsideration, the committee cannot find culpability if previously exonerated or impose a more severe penalty. Scope is restricted to GSAS; research misconduct is referred under Research Misconduct procedures; undergraduate cases follow separate Yale College Executive Committee procedures.

evidence.quote: Student statement. Students will be asked to respond in writing to the allegation. Providing a written statement allows the student to present their perspective on events and any broader context or other information that will help the Coordinating Group and committee to better understand the situation. Written statements will ordinarily be due to the secretary two weeks after the student receives notification of the charge. In their statement, students should admit or deny allegations against them. In some cases, the student may admit responsibility for some portion of the allegations and deny others.
evidence.location: Procedures: Student statement response deadline

evidence.quote: A hearing panel will have a minimum of four members, including the secretary (or dean’s designate) who does not typically vote. Voting members of the panel must include the chair or vice chair, one faculty member and/or dean of the graduate school, and one student member. The presence of three voting members will constitute a quorum, provided that at least one student member is present. A majority vote will decide questions before the hearing panel. In the event of a tie vote, the secretary or other committee designee will cast a deciding vote.
evidence.location: Procedures: Section A.2.c Hearing panel & quorum

evidence.quote: Determination. At the conclusion of the hearing, the committee will meet in an executive session to decide whether the conduct reported in fact occurred and whether it contravened the standards cited in the charge. The committee’s decision will be made by a simple majority of voting members present. The secretary will vote only in the event of a tie. This decision will be made by a preponderance of the evidence, voted on by secret ballot, and will be final.
evidence.location: Procedures: Section C.8 Determination & quorum voting

evidence.quote: If the committee decides that the conduct reported occurred and that it contravened the standards cited in the charge, based on the seriousness of the contravention, the committee will also recommend a sanction, if any, to the dean. The dean may either impose the recommended sanction or a lesser or greater one at their discretion.
evidence.location: Procedures: Section C.8 Sanction recommendation to dean

evidence.quote: The Committee of Review will receive written appeals from a student or students who have been assigned a penalty. An appeal must be received by the Committee of Review no later than five business days after the decision of the committee and may be sent to the secretary. To review such appeals, the Committee of Review will have access to all the written records of the committee.
evidence.location: Procedures: Section C.10.2 Appeal deadline to Committee of Review

Permissibility of AI writing tools varies from course to course and across research settings; graduate students are responsible for consulting relevant faculty members before using AI tools for coursework or research.

scope.en: Guidelines for AI in studying and teaching; LEX 1.3.3 directive on citing and distinguishing borrowed material (French text is binding; English is a reference translation, with an unresolved Version xx. footer placeholder); rules for continuous assessment; Library AI advice. scope.zh: 学习与教学中使用 AI 的指引；LEX 1.3.3 引文及区分借用内容指令（法文文本具约束力，英文为参考译文，其 Version xx. 页脚占位标识尚未解决）；平时考核规则；图书馆 AI 指导。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: EPFL guidelines for using AI in studying advise students that they should not use AI during exams or assessments unless explicitly allowed, and tell students to check their course policy or ask their instructor. Assessment material that is not the student's personal and original contribution must be recognizable as such under LEX 1.3.3 Article 4; guidelines advise disclosing AI-tool use in a statement and checking the course policy or instructor for its formulation.
coursework.zh: EPFL 学习使用 AI 指引建议学生，除非明确允许，否则在考试或考核中不应使用 AI，并告知学生核对课程规定或咨询教师。依据 Lex 1.3.3 第 4 条，非学生本人原创贡献的考核材料必须可被识别；指引建议在声明中披露 AI 工具的使用，并查阅课程规定或教师要求确定表述方式。

For manuscripts intended for publication, EPFL Library guidance states that the LLM used, what it was used for, and how it was used must be disclosed in the manuscript, adhering to publisher policies.
disclosure.zh: EPFL 学习指引指出，依据 Lex 1.3.3 第 4 条，非学生个人原创贡献的考核材料必须清晰可辨，表示应（should）在声明中披露 AI 工具的使用，并指引学生核对课程具体 AI 规定或咨询教师如何表述。对于拟发表的手稿，EPFL 图书馆指引规定必须（must）在手稿中披露所使用的 LLM、具体用途及使用方式，并遵守所选出版机构的相关政策。

privacy_data.en: EPFL advises students not to input confidential, private, or personal information into public generative AI tools because data is shared with private companies and control is lost. In the captured EPFL teaching guide, enterprise licenses such as Microsoft 365 Copilot via an EPFL account are described as unsuitable for regulated data because the guide states that EPFL has not signed a data processing agreement guaranteeing protections aligned with institutional needs or Swiss personal-data legislation; the current central-IT contract or tenant DPA status was not independently established in this review.
privacy_data.zh: EPFL 建议学生切勿将机密、隐私或个人信息输入外部公开生成式 AI 工具，因为数据将与私营企业共享且失去控制。在已采集的 EPFL 教学指引中，通过 EPFL 账户使用的企业许可（如 Microsoft 365 Copilot）被描述为不适合处理受监管数据，因为该指引称 EPFL 尚未签署确保数据保护措施符合机构需求或瑞士个人数据保护法的数据处理协议（DPA）；本次审查未独立核实当前中央 IT 合同或租户 DPA 状态。

research_publication.en: EPFL Library guidance clarifies that LLMs cannot be listed as authors or co-authors under the Swiss Copyright Act (Art. 6) because they lack accountability. Under EPFL Library's agreement with Elsevier, CC-BY open access content may be used with any AI tool, whereas for licensed closed or CC-BY-NC-ND publications, use is permitted with closed non-learning AI tools or with open learning tools operating in a secure, user-controlled environment (on-premises or solely for authorized users); commercial use is prohibited and publications must not reproduce closed or CC-BY-NC-ND content.
research_publication.zh: EPFL 图书馆指引明确说明，依据瑞士著作权法（第 6 条），LLM 因无法承担责任而不能列为作者或合著者。依据 EPFL 图书馆与 Elsevier 的协议，CC-BY 开放获取成果可用于任何 AI 工具；而对于订阅期刊受限内容或 CC-BY-NC-ND 成果，仅允许在不参与训练的封闭式 AI 工具中或在用户控制的安全受控环境（本地自建或仅限授权用户）中运行的学习型工具中使用；禁止商业用途，且生成结果不得复制封闭或 CC-BY-NC-ND 原文内容。

academic_integrity.en: Submitting AI-generated content as one's own work without proper attribution constitutes AI plagiarism under Lex 1.3.3 Article 4. AI detection tools are not admissible as stand-alone evidence due to false-positive risks; teacher referral of suspected non-disclosure to the section director and Legal Affairs is a misconduct evaluation referral, not an adjudication of cheating. Formal grade or notified failure disputes follow EPFL study regulations: internal reassessment within 10 days or external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days calculated from postal reception of the grade or notified failure; these rules govern academic grading disputes, and whether specific appeal pathways apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is an unverified evidence gap.
academic_integrity.zh: 依据 Lex 1.3.3 第 4 条，将 AI 生成内容作为本人作品提交且未适当归属构成 AI 抄袭。因存在较高误报风险，AI 检测工具不能单独作为抄袭证据；教师对疑似未披露情况向系主任及法务部门的报告属于行为性质评估移送，而非直接认定作弊。正式成绩或不及格通知争议遵循 EPFL 学习管理规定：在收到学业成绩或不及格书面邮寄通知后 10 天内申请校内重评，或 30 天内向 EPF 内部申诉委员会提出外部申诉；此程序适用于学业成绩争议，针对 AI 纪律处分的具体申诉途径仍属未核实的证据缺口。

topicBasis.research_publication: EPFL Library guidance clarifies that LLMs cannot be listed as authors or co-authors under the Swiss Copyright Act (Art. 6) because they lack accountability. Under EPFL Library's agreement with Elsevier, CC-BY open access content may be used with any AI tool, whereas for licensed closed or CC-BY-NC-ND publications, use is permitted with closed non-learning AI tools or with open learning tools operating in a secure, user-controlled environment (on-premises or solely for authorized users); commercial use is prohibited and publications must not reproduce closed or CC-BY-NC-ND content.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Submitting AI-generated content as one's own work without proper attribution constitutes AI plagiarism under Lex 1.3.3 Article 4. AI detection tools are not admissible as stand-alone evidence due to false-positive risks; teacher referral of suspected non-disclosure to the section director and Legal Affairs is a misconduct evaluation referral, not an adjudication of cheating. Formal grade or notified failure disputes follow EPFL study regulations: internal reassessment within 10 days or external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days calculated from postal reception of the grade or notified failure; these rules govern academic grading disputes, and whether specific appeal pathways apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is an unverified evidence gap.

do.en: Check course outlines and consult instructors regarding permitted AI use before using tools for studying or coursework.
do.zh: 在将生成式 AI 用于学习或课程作业前，查阅课程大纲并咨询任课教师以确认许可范围。

do.en: Ensure assessment material that is not your personal and original contribution is recognizable as such under LEX 1.3.3 Article 4; the studying guide says AI tool use should be disclosed in a statement and directs students to check the course policy or instructor for its formulation.
do.zh: 依据 Lex 1.3.3 第 4 条确保非本人原创贡献的考核材料清晰可辨；学习指引表示应在声明中披露 AI 工具使用，并指引学生查阅课程规定或咨询教师确定表述方式。

do.en: For manuscripts intended for publication, disclose the LLM tool used, its purpose, and method in the manuscript adhering to publisher policies.
do.zh: 对于拟发表的手稿，依据图书馆指引在手稿中披露所使用的 LLM 工具、具体用途及使用方式，并遵守出版社规定。

do.en: For disputes over an academic grade or notified failure, request internal reassessment within 10 days or appeal to the EPF internal appeals commission within 30 days, both from postal receipt at the student’s address. These deadlines have not been verified as AI disciplinary appeal deadlines.
do.zh: 对于学业成绩或不及格通知的争议，可在邮寄通知送达学生地址并收悉后 10 天内申请校内重评，或在收悉后 30 天内向 EPF 内部申诉委员会申诉。这些期限未被核实为 AI 纪律处分的申诉期限。

dont.en: Students should not use generative AI tools during exams or assessments unless explicitly allowed by the course policy or instructor.
dont.zh: 学生在考试或考核中不应使用生成式 AI，除非课程规定或教师明确允许。

dont.en: Do not enter confidential, personal, or regulated data into public AI tools; in the captured teaching guide, enterprise Microsoft 365 Copilot is described as unsuitable for regulated data because the guide states EPFL has not signed an aligned DPA, while current central-IT contract or tenant DPA status was not independently established.
dont.zh: 切勿将机密、个人或受监管数据输入公开 AI 工具；在已采集的教学指引中，企业版 Microsoft 365 Copilot 因指引称 EPFL 未签署对齐的 DPA 而被描述为不适合受监管数据，当前中央 IT 合同或租户 DPA 状态未独立核实。

dont.en: Do not list Large Language Models as authors or co-authors on manuscripts intended for publication.
dont.zh: 切勿在拟发表的手稿中将大型语言模型列为作者或合著者。

CL-005.text: In the captured EPFL teaching guide, enterprise licenses such as Microsoft 365 Copilot via an EPFL account are described as unsuitable for regulated data because the guide states that EPFL has not signed a data processing agreement guaranteeing protections aligned with institutional needs or Swiss personal-data legislation. The current central-IT contract or tenant DPA status was not independently established in this review.

evidence.quote: However, enterprise licenses such as Microsoft 365 Copilot via your EPFL account are currently not a secure solution for processing regulated data, because no data processing agreement has been signed by EPFL that would guarantee that data protection measures align with institutional needs or with Swiss legislation on personal data protection.
evidence.location: lines 89-89; Data Protection

draft-claim-epfl-library-licensed-conten.text: According to EPFL Library's description of its agreement with Elsevier, open access publications with a CC-BY license may be used with any available AI tool, including for tool development and training, with free sharing of results. For licensed closed publications or Open Access publications under a restrictive CC-BY-NC-ND license where Elsevier owns all or key rights, use is permitted with closed versions of AI tools that do not train the algorithm or learn from/incorporate inputs (e.g. non-learning ChatGPT Team, potentially subject to fees/restrictions), or with open versions of learning AI tools or institutional tool/platform development provided they operate in a secure, user-controlled environment (self-hosted on-premises or externally hosted solely for Participating Institutions or Authorized Users). AI-generated results or platforms may be published for research and teaching provided they do not contain or reproduce closed or CC-BY-NC-ND content (linking is permitted), while commercial use of such AI-generated content or platforms is prohibited.

draft-claim-epfl-grade-reassessment-appe.text: EPFL study management regulations provide two formal procedures to oppose a grade or notified failure: an internal request for reassessment at EPFL within 10 days, or an external appeal to the Commission de recours interne des EPF within 30 days. Both deadlines are calculated from reception, at the address given by the student, of the grade or notified failure (transcripts sent by post). If a mark is contested on the grounds of an error in correction or assessment, the responsible teacher is the only person authorized to modify the mark subject to justification to the program direction; if contested for a formal defect, Legal Affairs reviews whether a significant formal defect impacted the result to warrant exam cancellation and repetition. Procedural costs are charged ahead of the procedure and refunded only if the student's claim succeeds. These rules govern academic grade disputes; whether specific appeal pathways or different deadlines apply to AI disciplinary misconduct sanctions is not established on this page and remains an evidence gap.

evidence.quote: There are two ways of opposing a grade or notified failure: a procedure at EPFL, called request for reassessment, and a procedure outside of EPFL, through the Commission de recours interne des EPF, called appeal.
evidence.location: lines 58-58; Reassessment request and appeal

evidence.quote: The deadline to start these procedures is within 10 days for the request for reassessment and within 30 days for the appeal. Both deadlines are calculated from the reception, at the address given by the student, of the grade or notified failure (transcripts sent by post).
evidence.location: lines 61-61; Reassessment request and appeal / Deadlines

evidence.quote: If a mark is contested on the grounds of an error in correction or assessment, the teacher responsible will be asked to check the correction. He/she is the only person authorized to make any corrections. If he/she modifies the mark, he/she must justify the modification to the program’s direction, who will check whether the reason is justified. If the result is contested on the grounds of a formal defect, the matter is referred to Legal Affairs, who can only conclude that the examination should be cancelled if the formal defect is significant and has been shown to have had an impact on the result.
evidence.location: lines 59-59; Reassessment request and appeal / Grounds

evidence.quote: The costs are charged ahead of the procedure by EPFL and the appeals authority. They are refunded only if the student’s claim succeeds.
evidence.location: lines 60-60; Reassessment request and appeal / Costs

CL-004.text: EPFL guidance specifies that submitting AI-generated content as one's own work without proper attribution is considered AI plagiarism. Tools specifically aiming to detect AI-generated content are not admissible as stand-alone evidence of AI plagiarism due to a high risk of false positives. Under continuous assessment procedures, where unauthorized AI use or non-disclosure is suspected, the course teacher writes a report and submits it with evidence to the section director and Legal Service (Affaires juridiques) for formal evaluation, which constitutes a referral of suspected misconduct rather than an adjudication of cheating.

evidence.quote: Submitting AI-generated content as your own work without proper attribution is considered AI plagiarism.
evidence.location: lines 90-90; Transparency / What you should avoid

evidence.quote: Tools that specifically aim to detect whether content was AI-generated (e.g., turnitin) are not admissible as stand-alone evidence of AI plagiarism due to their high risk of false positives (e.g., Farrelly & Baker, 2023). Other irrefutable evidence must be presented to substantiate claims of academic dishonesty.
evidence.location: lines 98-98; AI plagiarism

evidence.quote: Use of AI tools in ways that are not authorized or failure to attribute their use will be treated as a potential case of cheating and will be forwarded to the EPFL Legal Affairs team
evidence.location: lines 53-53; Setting clear expectations

evidence.quote: In the case of any suspected fraud and/or cheating, the teacher writes a report which they then send to the section director and Legal Service together with evidence of the compromising or suspected item or behaviour.

scope.en: TUM ProLehre Didactic Guidance; APSO 12th Amending Statute Reading Version (Latest listed amendment 16 Dec 2025; formally published enactments remain legally authoritative); SGwP Research Statute; MKT Chair Thesis Guidelines. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: TUM ProLehre 教学指引；APSO 第 12 次修订规程阅读整理本（最新登载修订 2025 年 12 月 16 日；正式公布规程具法定效力）；SGwP 科研规范条例；MKT 教席论文规范。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: TUM ProLehre student guidance specifies that generative AI tools may be used for written coursework, term papers, essays, and theses only when AI tool use is explicitly permitted for that specific assessment by the instructor or module specifications. Where instructions are silent, students should ask in advance rather than assuming permission. When authorized, transparent documentation of tool use and prompts is commonly required, and students retain full personal responsibility for submitted work.
coursework.zh: TUM ProLehre 学生指引明确：仅在授课教师或模块说明对具体考核明确允许时，方可在课程论文、随堂作业、文章及学位论文中使用生成式 AI。若未作说明，学生应在提交前主动咨询确认，不可假定允许。经授权使用时，通常须如实记录所用工具及提示词，学生对提交成果承担全部个人责任。
coursework.meaningEn: TUM ProLehre student guidance on AI use in written coursework and thesis writing.
coursework.meaningZh: TUM ProLehre 关于课程书面作业与学位论文中 AI 使用的学生指引。

exams.en: Examinations prohibit unauthorized generative AI assistance. Under the reviewed APSO reading version, suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under APSO § 24(6), an examination failed due to § 22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. Severe or repeated deception or disruption may lead to degree-program exclusion under § 22(3); these are general examination provisions rather than an AI-specific sanction schedule.
exams.zh: 考试严禁未经授权的生成式 AI 辅助。依所审查的 APSO 阅读整理本，可使用适用软件检查未注明的文本或来源，并由考官判定是否存在欺骗作弊行为。依据 APSO 第 24(6) 条，因第 22 条欺骗或扰乱考场而未通过的考试仅可补考一次。严重或屡次欺骗扰乱者，依据第 22(3) 条可被处以终止修读该学位项目的处分；以上均为通用考试规程，而非特定于 AI 的单独制裁条款。
exams.meaningEn: TUM APSO examination regulations (§ 21, § 22, § 24) on deception, software detection, retakes, and procedural objections.
exams.meaningZh: TUM APSO 考试规程（第 21、22、24 条）关于作弊欺骗、软件检测、重考限制及程序异议的规定。

disclosure.en: When generative AI tool use is authorized, transparent documentation of tool use, methods, and prompts is commonly required and course-conditioned; students retain full personal responsibility for all submitted work. The Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research guidelines require a signed AI declaration for theses and seminar papers, including a formal non-use declaration if no AI was used.
disclosure.zh: 经授权使用生成式 AI 工具时，通常须按课程具体要求如实透明记录所用工具、方法与提示词；学生对所提交的全部成果承担完全个人责任。市场与消费研究教席（MKT）指南要求在学位论文与研讨课论文中插入签名版 AI 声明；若未曾使用，须提交正式的未曾使用声明。
disclosure.meaningEn: TUM ProLehre coursework documentation guidance and MKT Chair thesis declaration requirements.
disclosure.meaningZh: TUM ProLehre 课程作业记录指引与 MKT 教席论文声明要求。

privacy_data.en: TUM ProLehre guidance instructs students and instructors not to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools, which applies also to TUM-approved systems. In addition, teaching and study materials (such as lecture slides, scripts, recordings, or past exams) are protected intellectual property and require explicit instructor consent before being uploaded to or processed in AI tools, even when used solely for personal study purposes like summarization, transcription, or translation.
privacy_data.zh: TUM ProLehre 指引要求师生切勿将个人数据、敏感信息或机密材料输入 AI 工具，该禁令同样适用于 TUM 批准的系统。此外，教学与研习材料（如讲义课件、讲稿、录音录像或历年考题）受知识产权保护，即便利于个人学习目的（如总结、听写或翻译），亦须事先获得授课教师的明确许可方可上传至 AI 工具进行处理。
privacy_data.meaningEn: TUM ProLehre guidance on personal data protection (including approved tools) and copyright consent for teaching materials.
privacy_data.meaningZh: TUM ProLehre 关于个人数据保护（含已批准工具）及课件教材版权许可的指引。

approved_tools.en: TUM provides M365 Copilot Chat through TUMonline activation, but tool activation does not establish assessment permission or authorization to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data. ProLehre highlights Chat-AI by AcademicCloud as a privacy-friendly option hosted on German university servers, but reviewed sources do not establish individual account eligibility or licensing guarantees.
approved_tools.zh: TUM 通过 TUMonline 激活提供 M365 Copilot Chat，但激活工具绝不构成考核使用许可，亦不授权输入个人、敏感或机密数据。ProLehre 推荐由德国高校服务器托管的 AcademicCloud Chat-AI 作为保护隐私的备选方案，但所审查的官方材料并未确认个人账户资格或授权许可保证。
approved_tools.meaningEn: TUM digitalization announcement for M365 Copilot Chat and ProLehre recommendation for AcademicCloud Chat-AI.
approved_tools.meaningZh: TUM 关于 M365 Copilot Chat 的数字化公告及 ProLehre 针对 AcademicCloud Chat-AI 的教学推荐。

research_publication.en: TUM SGwP statutes establish research integrity standards requiring research data retention on durable secure media, ordinarily for 10 years from publication unless justified shorter periods or discipline-specific standards apply. Guidelines from the MKT Chair permit AI as a research aid for theses but prohibit AI empirical data collection and analysis unless explicitly approved by the supervisor.
research_publication.zh: TUM SGwP 科研规范条例确立了学术诚信标准，要求将科研数据保存在安全持久的介质上，自发表之日起通常保存 10 年，除非具备正当理由缩短期限或适用特定学科标准。MKT 教席指引允许将 AI 作为论文的研究辅助工具，但严禁将 AI 用于实证数据收集与分析，获导师明确批准者除外。
research_publication.meaningEn: TUM SGwP research integrity statute (data retention) and MKT Chair thesis research rules.
research_publication.meaningZh: TUM SGwP 科研诚信条例（数据保存）及 MKT 教席论文研究规范。

academic_integrity.en: Under the reviewed APSO reading version, attempted deception in examinations or coursework results in an assessment grade of 5.0 (fail). A failed examination resulting from deception or disruption may be retaken only once under § 24(6). Under § 25(3), a candidate may inspect examination files upon reasoned written application to the examination board chair within 1 month of grade announcement, with time and place determined by the chair with the examiner. Under § 21, procedural defects must be raised promptly in writing. Formally published enactments remain legally authoritative over the reading consolidation. The inspection window is not a deadline for disciplinary or administrative appeals, which remain unreviewed.
academic_integrity.zh: 依所审查的 APSO 阅读整理本，在考试或作业中企图欺骗作弊将导致该考核评定为 5.0（不合格）。因欺骗或扰乱考场而未通过的考试依第 24(6) 条仅可补考一次。依第 25(3) 条，考生可在成绩公布后 1 个月内向考试委员会主席提交附具理由的书面申请查阅试卷档案，具体时间地点由委员会主席与考官共同确定。依第 21 条，考核程序瑕疵必须及时书面提出。正式公布的规程文本较阅读整理本具有法定效力。 此查阅期限并非纪律或行政申诉期限，后者仍未审查。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: TUM APSO § 22 misconduct, § 24 retakes, § 25 examination file inspection, and § 21 procedural objections.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: TUM APSO 第 22 条不端行为、第 24 条重考、第 25 条查阅试卷档案及第 21 条程序异议规定。

topicBasis.coursework: TUM ProLehre student guidance specifies that generative AI tools may be used for written coursework, term papers, essays, and theses only when AI tool use is explicitly permitted for that specific assessment by the instructor or module specifications. Where instructions are silent, students should ask in advance rather than assuming permission. When authorized, transparent documentation of tool use and prompts is commonly required, and students retain full personal responsibility for submitted work.
topicBasis.exams: Examinations prohibit unauthorized generative AI assistance. Under the reviewed APSO reading version, suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under APSO § 24(6), an examination failed due to § 22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. Severe or repeated deception or disruption may lead to degree-program exclusion under § 22(3); these are general examination provisions rather than an AI-specific sanction schedule.
topicBasis.disclosure: When generative AI tool use is authorized, transparent documentation of tool use, methods, and prompts is commonly required and course-conditioned; students retain full personal responsibility for all submitted work. The Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research guidelines require a signed AI declaration for theses and seminar papers, including a formal non-use declaration if no AI was used.
topicBasis.privacy_data: TUM ProLehre guidance instructs students and instructors not to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools, which applies also to TUM-approved systems. In addition, teaching and study materials (such as lecture slides, scripts, recordings, or past exams) are protected intellectual property and require explicit instructor consent before being uploaded to or processed in AI tools, even when used solely for personal study purposes like summarization, transcription, or translation.
topicBasis.approved_tools: TUM provides M365 Copilot Chat through TUMonline activation, but tool activation does not establish assessment permission or authorization to enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data. ProLehre highlights Chat-AI by AcademicCloud as a privacy-friendly option hosted on German university servers, but reviewed sources do not establish individual account eligibility or licensing guarantees.
topicBasis.research_publication: TUM SGwP statutes establish research integrity standards requiring research data retention on durable secure media, ordinarily for 10 years from publication unless justified shorter periods or discipline-specific standards apply. Guidelines from the MKT Chair permit AI as a research aid for theses but prohibit AI empirical data collection and analysis unless explicitly approved by the supervisor.
topicBasis.academic_integrity: Under the reviewed APSO reading version, attempted deception in examinations or coursework results in an assessment grade of 5.0 (fail). A failed examination resulting from deception or disruption may be retaken only once under § 24(6). Under § 25(3), a candidate may inspect examination files upon reasoned written application to the examination board chair within 1 month of grade announcement, with time and place determined by the chair with the examiner. Under § 21, procedural defects must be raised promptly in writing. Formally published enactments remain legally authoritative over the reading consolidation. The inspection window is not a deadline for disciplinary or administrative appeals, which remain unreviewed.

do.en: Check coursework instructions: only use generative AI tools when explicitly permitted for that specific assessment; ask the instructor in advance if instructions are silent.
do.zh: 查阅课程具体说明：仅在相应考核明确允许时方可使用生成式 AI 工具；若说明未提及，应事先向授课教师咨询确认。

do.en: When authorized, transparently document AI tools, methods, and prompts according to course instructions, and obtain explicit instructor consent before uploading any teaching or study materials.
do.zh: 经授权使用时，按照课程要求如实透明记录所用 AI 工具、方法与提示词；上传任何课件或研习材料前须取得授课教师明确许可。

do.en: For exam inspections under APSO § 25(3), submit a reasoned written application to the examination board chair within 1 month of grade announcement; the chair determines place and time with the examiner.
do.zh: 若依据 APSO 第 25(3) 条申请试卷查阅，须在成绩公布后 1 个月内向考试委员会主席提交附具理由的书面申请；委员会主席与考官共同确定查阅时间与地点。

dont.en: Do not use generative AI in examinations or written coursework without explicit permission; unauthorized use may be treated as deception under APSO § 22, where retakes are limited to one.
dont.zh: 未经明确许可，切勿在考试或书面作业中使用生成式 AI；擅自使用可依 APSO 第 22 条被视为欺骗行为，且重考仅限一次。

dont.en: Do not enter personal, sensitive, or confidential data into AI tools (including TUM-approved systems), and do not upload teaching materials without explicit instructor consent even for personal study.
dont.zh: 切勿将个人、敏感或机密数据输入 AI 工具（包括 TUM 批准的系统），未经教师明确许可切勿上传课件教学材料（即使仅用于个人学习）。

dont.en: Do not assume institutional tool access (such as M365 Copilot Chat or AcademicCloud Chat-AI) confers permission for specific course assessments or thesis submissions.
dont.zh: 切勿将开通 M365 Copilot Chat 或使用 AcademicCloud Chat-AI 等校内工具等同于获准将其用于具体考核或学位论文。

draft-claim-tum-apso-misconduct-and-reta.text: In the APSO reading version as amended by the12th amending statute, §22(1) says attempting to influence an examination result through deception or unauthorized aids leads to a failing grade. Suitable software may check unacknowledged text or sources, while the examiner determines whether deception occurred. Under §22(2), disruption may lead to exclusion from that examination and a failing grade. In serious or repeated deception or disruption cases, the examination committee may exclude the student from further examinations in the degree program, with final failure of the degree examination (§22(3)). Under §24(6), an examination failed because of §22 deception or disruption may be retaken only once. These are general examination provisions, not a separate AI-specific sanction schedule.

draft-claim-tum-mkt-chair-thesis-ai-decl.text: The Guidelines for Writing Theses and Seminar Papers (Juli 2026) issued by the TUM Chair of Marketing and Consumer Research permit the use of generative AI tools (such as ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity) as research aids for seminar, Bachelor's, and Master's theses, subject to mandatory declaration inserted before the bibliography. The declaration requires students to specify the exact tools used and the specific tasks performed (brainstorming, literature search, structuring, code generation, hypothesis generation, translation, image generation, or language improvement), and confirm that they personally reviewed the entire thesis and accept full responsibility. If no AI tools were used, a formal non-use statement must be included ('Ich habe keine generativen KI-Tools oder -Hilfsmittel verwendet.'). AI-generated images must cite the specific tool, and the use of AI for empirical data collection and analysis is prohibited for data protection reasons unless explicitly approved by the thesis supervisor. These are the reviewed chair guidelines; no broader TUM rule established.

draft-claim-tum-sgwp-research-integrity-.text: The reviewed TUM-SGwP statute requires researchers working at TUM to follow recognized scientific standards, document work, question results and act honestly (§1). Supervisors must verifiably give the statute to students conducting scientific thesis work (§22). Under §8, primary and evaluated data and evaluation software used for publications must be kept on durable secure media in the originating institution; retention depends on discipline and is ordinarily ten years from the relevant publication, with reasons for non-retention or shorter periods documented. Authorship requires a genuine, traceable contribution and honorary authorship is prohibited (§12). Under §13, scientific misconduct involves knowingly or grossly negligently making false statements, violating others' intellectual property or impairing their research in a scientifically relevant context. Anyone may approach the ombudsperson concerning suspected misconduct (§16).

scope.en: Johns Hopkins IT Responsible Use & Data Governance; Teaching @ JHU & CTEI Guidance; Whiting Engineering for Professionals (EP) Course Categorization & Student AI Guide; Krieger/Whiting Graduate Academic Misconduct Procedures (Homewood 2017 / AAP 2018); Hopkins Press Author Policy. Institution audit remains PARTIAL.
scope.zh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯 IT 负责任使用与数据治理；Teaching @ JHU 与 CTEI 教学指引；怀廷工程继续教育（EP）课程分类与学生 AI 指引；克里格/怀廷研究生学术不端处理程序（霍姆伍德 2017 / AAP 2018）；霍普金斯大学出版社作者政策。全校审计状态保持 PARTIAL。

coursework.en: Engineering for Professionals (EP) implements a course-level color classification system for generative AI use: Red (no AI permitted in any form), Yellow (moderate AI permitted with restrictions and required disclosure), and Green (liberal AI permitted with transparency). Course-level designation is mandatory; Yellow courses must also include assignment-level labels. This policy applies strictly to EP courses and does not establish a blanket university-wide permission.
coursework.zh: 工程专业继续教育（EP）实行课程级 AI 颜色分类体系：红色（禁止以任何形式使用 AI）、黄色（在限制条件下适度使用且必须披露）、绿色（广泛使用但须保持透明）。课程级标识为强制要求；黄色课程考核须逐项标明分类。该政策仅适用于 EP 课程，不构成全校通用许可。
coursework.meaningEn: Whiting School of Engineering for Professionals (EP) course color classification policy.
coursework.meaningZh: 怀廷工程学院继续教育（EP）课程颜色分类政策。

exams.en: In Engineering for Professionals (EP) courses, assessments designated Red strictly prohibit generative AI assistance in any form. Students must follow specific course and examination instructions; tool access does not confer examination permission, and unauthorized AI use is subject to disciplinary procedures.
exams.zh: 在工程专业继续教育（EP）课程中，标明红色（Red）的考核严禁使用任何形式的生成式 AI 辅助。学生必须遵守具体课程与考试说明；开通工具不代表获得考试使用许可，擅自使用将按纪律程序处理。
exams.meaningEn: Engineering for Professionals (EP) Red assessment classification and examination rules.
exams.meaningZh: 工程专业继续教育（EP）红色考核分类与考试规定。

disclosure.en: In Yellow and Green EP courses, students must adhere to instructor standards for AI disclosure, where full transcripts, model/site citations, or visual highlighting serve as potential examples. Students must save AI outputs and interaction records if disclosure or verification is requested by the course. Hopkins Press requires authors to disclose generative AI use in submissions and will not credit AI as an author.
disclosure.zh: 在黄色与绿色 EP 课程中，学生必须遵循授课教师的 AI 披露标准，完整对话记录、模型/网址引用或视觉标记均为可选示例。若课程或教师要求披露或核验，学生必须留存 AI 输出与交互记录。霍普金斯出版社要求作者在投稿中披露生成式 AI 的使用，且不将 AI 列为作者。
disclosure.meaningEn: EP student disclosure standards, record retention requirements, and Hopkins Press author policy.
disclosure.meaningZh: EP 学生披露标准、记录留存要求及霍普金斯大学出版社作者政策。

privacy_data.en: Johns Hopkins IT policies prohibit entering non-public proprietary Hopkins data (including clinical, financial, and business records) into unapproved third-party AI tools. Meeting hosts should not enable Zoom AI Companion features for meetings involving student education records (FERPA recommendation). HopGPT is approved for sensitive data including PHI and PII, subject to institutional stewardship and required research approvals (IRB for non-clinical research; SIP for clinical research or uses involving PHI/PII).
privacy_data.zh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯 IT 政策禁止将非公开专有数据（包括临床、财务和商务记录）输入未经批准的第三方 AI 工具。若会议涉及学生教育记录（FERPA 建议），主持人不应开启 Zoom AI Companion 功能。HopGPT 经批准可处理包括 PHI 和 PII 在内的敏感数据，但须经机构管理并取得所需科研审批（非临床研究须经 IRB 审批；临床研究或涉及 PHI/PII 的使用须经 SIP 审批）。
privacy_data.meaningEn: Johns Hopkins IT data governance (confidential data ban), HopGPT research branches, and Zoom AI FERPA recommendation.
privacy_data.meaningZh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯 IT 数据治理（机密数据禁令）、HopGPT 科研分支及 Zoom AI FERPA 建议。

approved_tools.en: Johns Hopkins provides ChatGPT Edu ($8.50/mo base plus usage for full-time faculty/staff), HopGPT (secure internal LLM), Copilot Web (free, non-HIPAA), Microsoft 365 Copilot ($215/yr, HIPAA-compliant), Claude ($22/$55 recharge for active affiliates 18+ on campus or VPN), and Zoom AI Companion (hosts should not enable for FERPA student records). Institutional tool access does not confer coursework or exam authorization.
approved_tools.zh: 霍普金斯提供 ChatGPT Edu（专职教职工每月 8.50 美元起加用量费）、HopGPT（安全校内大模型）、Copilot 网页版（免费、非 HIPAA）、Microsoft 365 Copilot（每年 215 美元、符合 HIPAA）、Claude（面向有效所属成员且年满 18 岁的 22/55 美元内部转账，申请须使用校园网络或 VPN）及 Zoom AI Companion（涉及 FERPA 学生记录时不建议开启）。开通校内工具不等于课程或考试使用许可。
approved_tools.meaningEn: Enterprise tool offerings (ChatGPT Edu, HopGPT, Copilot Web, M365 Copilot, Claude, Zoom AI Companion) and authorization boundaries.
approved_tools.meaningZh: 校内工具服务（ChatGPT Edu、HopGPT、Copilot 网页版、M365 Copilot、Claude、Zoom AI Companion）及授权边界。

research_publication.en: Hopkins Press policy requires authors to disclose generative AI use in publisher submissions; manuscripts substantially written by AI are not accepted. Research use of HopGPT requires IRB approval for non-clinical research and SIP approval for clinical research or uses involving PHI/PII.
research_publication.zh: 霍普金斯出版社政策要求作者在出版投稿中如实披露生成式 AI 使用；不接收实质由 AI 撰写的书稿。在科研中使用 HopGPT 时，非临床研究须经 IRB 审批，临床研究或涉及 PHI/PII 的使用须经 SIP 审批。
research_publication.meaningEn: Johns Hopkins University Press author policy and HopGPT IRB/SIP research governance.
research_publication.meaningZh: 约翰斯·霍普金斯大学出版社作者政策及 HopGPT IRB/SIP 科研治理。

academic_integrity.en: Under Graduate Academic Misconduct Procedures applying to KSAS and WSE (Homewood 2017 / AAP 2018), informal resolution of first offenses requires AIO consultation, sanction not exceeding course failure, and mutual agreement reported to the AIO. Hearing Panels apply the preponderance-of-the-evidence standard. Except for informal first-offense resolutions, appeals must be submitted in writing to the AIO or designee for the Cognizant Dean within 10 university business days of the date of the outcome notice, limited to material procedural error, new unavailable information, or excessive sanction. Appeals involve a file review rather than another hearing. CTEI detector guidance is instructional advice rather than a university-wide ban.
academic_integrity.zh: 依适用于 KSAS 与 WSE 的研究生学术不端处理程序（霍姆伍德 2017 / AAP 2018），初次违规的非正式和解须事先咨询学术诚信官员（AIO）、处分不超过课程不及格且经双方同意并向 AIO 备案。听证委员会采用优势证据标准。除初次违规非正式和解外，申诉须在结果通知日期起 10 个大学工作日内书面提交 AIO 或指定人员转交主管院长，且仅限于重大程序错误、当时无法获取的新信息或处分过重。申诉为书面审查而非重新听证。CTEI 对检测工具的指引属于教学建议而非全校性禁令。
academic_integrity.meaningEn: Graduate Academic Misconduct Policy (KSAS/WSE Homewood 2017 & AAP 2018), 10-day appeal window, and CTEI detector guidance.
academic_integrity.meaningZh: 研究生学术不端处理政策（KSAS/WSE 霍姆伍德 2017 与 AAP 2018）、10 天申诉期及 CTEI 检测器指导意见。

draft-claim-jhu-press-author-ai-policy.text: Hopkins Press holds authors accountable for their work, does not permit AI or LLMs to be listed as authors, and will not accept work substantially written by an AI or LLM tool. Authors remain responsible for originality, accuracy, avoiding plagiarism and citing sources, including AI-generated content; they accept liability for AI use.

evidence.quote:
Authorship. Authors are accountable and legally responsible for the entirety of their work. Therefore, AI

publication. The Press will not accept any work that is substantially written by an AI or LLM tool.
